target.title: fix(control-ui): resolve Personal card avatar 401 via data URI
target.body: ## Problem Fixes #97602 The Personal card in Control UI shows a broken avatar image (401) because `agent.identity.get` returns `/avatar/` — a path requiring Bearer auth — while `agents.list` correctly resolves workspace-relative avatars to base64 data URIs. Since `` tags cannot carry Authorization headers, the Personal card always fails. ## Root Cause Two RPC handlers resolve agent avatars differently: | RPC | Avatar resolution | Result | |-----|-------------------|--------| | `agents.list` | `resolveIdentityAvatarUrl()` reads file → base64 data URI | ✅ Works | | `agent.identity.get` | `resolveAssistantAvatarUrl()` → `/avatar/` path | ❌ 401 | Additionally, the frontend (`app-render.ts`) explicitly constructs `/avatar/` via `buildAssistantAvatarRoute()` when `avatarStatus === "local"`, bypassing any data URI the backend might return. ## Changes ### 1. `src/gateway/session-utils.ts` - Export `resolveIdentityAvatarUrl` (was private) ### 2. `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts` - Import `resolveIdentityAvatarUrl` - In `agent.identity.get` handler, try `resolveIdentityAvatarUrl()` first (returns data URI for workspace-relative paths), falling back to `resolveAssistantAvatarUrl()` for other avatar types ### 3. `ui/src/ui/app-render.ts` - Remove `buildAssistantAvatarRoute()` call for local avatars in Personal card config - Use the data URI returned by the RPC (via `assistantAvatarUrl`) instead of constructing an unauthenticated URL path ## Testing Verified on OpenClaw 2026.6.10 (aa69b12): patched dist files locally, restarted gateway, hard-refreshed Control UI. Personal card avatar displays correctly — no more 401 on `/avatar/`.

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency.

Related: #97638

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled:

1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace.
2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts.
3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `<location>` paths). Skill names are XML-escaped. The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides.
4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution.

## User Impact

```json5
{
  agents: { defaults: { sandbox: {
    skipSkillsSync: true,
    docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" }
  } } }
}
```

Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (Docker container)

![sandbox-verify-e79a716](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/verify-skillsync-e79a716)

*Screenshot: terminal output from container with commit `e79a716ebe3`.*

```

}

```

### Test coverage (9 tests pass, 0 failures)

- drops host snapshot and builds name-only prompt when `skipSkillsSync` is enabled
- drops host snapshot (no remapping) when `skipSkillsSync` is absent (regression guard)
- keeps snapshots for non-sandboxed runs (regression guard)

target.title: fix(browser): handle Chrome launch stderr pipe errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts:launchOpenClawChrome` spawns Chrome with
`stdio: ["ignore", "ignore", "pipe"]` and attaches a `proc.stderr.on("data", ...)`
listener that buffers stderr chunks for launch-failure diagnostics. The listener
is registered and detached cleanly, but **no `error` listener is attached to
`proc.stderr`**. If the stderr pipe emits an `EPIPE` / `RST` (e.g. Chrome's
parent already exited and the kernel tore the pipe down before Chrome's own
exit handler ran), Node escalates the `error` event to an unhandled error that
crashes the gateway host — even though the child process itself is on its way
out and the launch-failure path would handle it correctly.

This is the same class of bug Alix-007 / cxbAsDev / steipete have been
canonically fixing across `file-transfer` (#101590), `discord` ffmpeg (#101124),
`google-meet` audio bridge (#101596, open), `matrix` deps (#101597, open),
`microsoft-foundry` az login (#101598, open), and `codex-supervisor` stdio
(#101599, open). It is a transport-layer unhandled-error family that Node
explicitly warns about, and the pattern is well-validated against the canonical
`proc.stderr.on("error", (err) => log.warn(...))` fix.

## Changes

- `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts`: import `formatErrorMessage`
  from `../infra/errors.js` and register a `proc.stderr.on("error", ...)`
  listener in `launchOnceAndWait`, immediately after the existing
  `proc.stderr.on("data", onStderr)` registration. The listener logs the
  pipe failure via `log.warn` and lets the existing launch-readiness
  kill / diagnostic flow continue.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts`: add a focused
  regression test that emits a synthetic `EPIPE` on the fake Chrome stderr
  stream after `launchOpenClawChrome` has registered its `error` listener.
  The test asserts that the launch-failure path still resolves with
  `/Failed to start Chrome CDP/` and that `proc.kill("SIGKILL")` was called.

This is the **symmetric counterpart to** the active stream-error campaign
PRs (#101590 #101124 #101596 #101597 #101598 #101599). It is **not** a
duplicate of #101506 (`mikasa0818`, "bound Chrome launch stderr diagnostics")
which fixes a *different* dimension — bounded 64 KiB tail retention at
the collection boundary. The two fixes are orthogonal: bounded-buffer
caps in-memory growth; this PR prevents unhandled-error crashes when the
pipe itself fails.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Chrome launch with a pipe failure on the stderr
  stream must not crash the gateway host. The launch-failure diagnostic
  path must still resolve, the child must be SIGKILL'd, and the failure
  must be reported via `log.warn`.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0,
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` against the production launch path with
  `child_process.spawn` mocked.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts -t "does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch"`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` (full file)
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
   ✓ chrome.ts internal > launchOpenClawChrome > does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed | 54 skipped (55)
     Start at  08:51:26
     Duration  16.67s
  ```
  Full file:
  ```
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  55 passed (55)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: The fixture EventEmitter starts with no
  `error` listener. The test hooks `fakeProc.stderr.on("newListener", ...)`
  to wait until `launchOpenClawChrome` has attached the production
  listener, then emits `new Error("EPIPE")` on stderr. The production
  listener routes the event through `log.warn`, the launch-readiness
  loop times out, `proc.kill("SIGKILL")` fires, and `launchOpenClawChrome`
  rejects with `Failed to start Chrome CDP on port 55558 for profile
  "openclaw-launch-XXXX". CDP diagnostic: http_unreachable after 2000ms;
  cdp=http://127.0.0.1:55558; ECONNREFUSED.` — matching the canonical
  sibling-fix shape.
- **Negative control** (proves the test exercises the fix, not a
  tautology): reverting only the `chrome.ts` change while keeping the
  new test makes the test time out at the 120s vitest default — the
  `error` event has no listener and Node escalates it to an unhandled
  crash that the test cannot recover from:
  ```
  $ timeout 130 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ...
  (terminated, exit 124)
  ```
- **What was not tested**:
  - Real Chrome process under controlled stderr EPIPE conditions (would
    require a daemonized Chrome + parent-exit harness; out of scope for
    a transport-layer listener fix).
  - Live CI on `openclaw/main` (the PR is pre-push; CI verification is
    expected to run on push).

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Chrome launch must not crash the gateway host
  when the spawned Chrome child's stderr pipe fails with `EPIPE` /
  `RST`. The fix adds the missing `error` listener that mirrors the
  pattern Alix-007 / cxbAsDev / steipete have shipped across
  `file-transfer`, `discord` ffmpeg, `google-meet`, `matrix`,
  `microsoft-foundry`, and `codex-supervisor`.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0,
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` driving `launchOpenClawChrome` with
  `child_process.spawn` mocked.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts -t "does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch"` → 1 passed
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` → 55/55 passed
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` → exit 0
  - `pnpm tsgo:extensions` → exit 0
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` → All matched files use the correct format
- **Evidence after fix**: 55/55 vitest tests pass; new test
  "does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch"
  passes (8.51s start, 16.67s duration). Negative control confirms the
  test exercises the production listener by reverting it and observing
  the test time out at 120s with exit 124.
- **Observed result after fix**: Launch-failure path still resolves
  with `Failed to start Chrome CDP ... ECONNREFUSED`; `proc.kill("SIGKILL")`
  fires; `proc.stderr` `error` listener routes through `log.warn`.
- **What was not tested**: Real Chrome stderr-pipe EPIPE under controlled
  Chrome + parent-exit harness (out of scope for a transport-layer
  listener fix).

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` —
  **55/55 passed** (12.91s start, 22.06s duration)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` — exit 0
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — exit 0
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on changed files — exit 0

Added tests:

- `does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch` —
  drives `launchOpenClawChrome` with `child_process.spawn` mocked,
  waits for the production `error` listener to attach (via the
  `EventEmitter.newListener` hook), emits a synthetic `EPIPE` on
  the fake stderr stream, and asserts that the launch-failure path
  still resolves with `/Failed to start Chrome CDP/` and that
  `proc.kill("SIGKILL")` fires. The test inverts to a 120s timeout
  when the production fix is reverted, proving the assertion exercises
  the new listener rather than a tautology.

## Risk checklist

- **Scope**: 2 files, 1 module (`chrome.ts:launchOpenClawChrome`); +11 prod, +53 test.
- **Behavior**: Old launch path unchanged. Only addition is the
  `error` listener on `proc.stderr`, which logs and lets the existing
  recovery flow continue.
- **API/signature changes**: none.
- **Type check**: `pnpm tsgo:extensions` exit 0.
- **Sibling PRs**: This is the **chrome.ts counterpart** to the active
  stream-error campaign: #101590 (file-transfer), #101124 (discord ffmpeg),
  #101596 (google-meet), #101597 (matrix), #101598 (microsoft-foundry),
  #101599 (codex-supervisor). It is **not** a duplicate of #101506
  (`mikasa0818`, "bound Chrome launch stderr diagnostics") which fixes a
  different dimension (bounded 64 KiB buffer tail vs stream `error`
  listener).

## Out of scope (separate follow-ups)

- The `bootstrap` spawn inside `launchOpenClawChrome` (line 1001) does
  not register a stderr `data` listener at all and is therefore not
  affected by the same `error`-listener gap; no change is required
  there. If a follow-up PR wants belt-and-braces coverage on the
  bootstrap path it can land independently.

target.title: fix(extensions): bound JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a malformed or unexpectedly large API response from external services (Feishu, Discord, Google Meet, Tlon) could cause the gateway process to buffer an arbitrarily large payload into memory, leading to an out-of-memory crash.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recent work bounded response reads across most extensions to prevent OOM from oversized API responses. Several extensions still used raw `response.json()` without size limits. This change replaces those calls with the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper, which caps reads at a safe limit. Existing error handling patterns (try/catch, .catch() fallbacks) are preserved.

## User Impact

Gateway operators running Feishu, Discord, Google Meet, or Tlon channel plugins are protected from OOM crashes caused by unexpectedly large external API responses.

## Evidence

All 1136 tests pass across 84 test files. Build succeeds. Terminal proof shows the bounded reader rejecting a 20MB response with "Discord PluralKit response: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes" while normal responses parse correctly.

target.title: feat(agents): add iteration budget for agent loop safety
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has heuristic loop detection and whole-run timeouts, but no explicit per-agent hard budget for LLM tool-calling rounds. Production reports show that some agent/model/channel combinations can keep calling tools after useful results are available, duplicate visible messages, or continue consuming model calls after lifecycle bugs.

This PR adds an opt-in circuit breaker for those cases. It is intentionally disabled by default and configurable per agent so long-horizon agents can keep larger budgets while high-risk chat/tool agents can be bounded.

Addresses: #6890, #75468, #89090, #79301, #75355, #77625, #74859, #82518

## Why This Change Was Made

The implementation adds:

- `agents.defaults.iterationBudget` and per-agent `agents.list[].iterationBudget` overrides.
- `enabled`, `maxIterations`, `subagentMaxIterations`, and `forceSummaryOnExhaustion` config fields.
- An `onBeforeToolCallingRound` agent-core hook that runs after a model emits tool calls but before those tools execute.
- Embedded-runner budget exhaustion handling that returns `budget_exhausted`.
- Harness opt-in via `supportsIterationBudget`, with built-in OpenClaw and Codex support.
- Fail-closed behavior when a selected harness does not support budget enforcement.

## User Impact

Default behavior is unchanged because the budget is disabled unless configured. When enabled, the budget caps LLM tool-calling rounds, not individual tool calls and not total long-horizon task duration. A single model response containing multiple tool calls counts as one round.

Operators can use this as a safety net for agents where runaway tool loops are more harmful than stopping early. Long-horizon agents should either leave the budget disabled or set an intentionally higher per-agent limit.

## Evidence

### Real configured OpenClaw run proof

Ran a real local OpenClaw CLI agent turn through `openclaw agent --local --json`
with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and a
temporary workspace. The config selected an OpenAI-compatible local provider and
enabled:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "iterationBudget": {
        "enabled": true,
        "maxIterations": 2,
        "forceSummaryOnExhaustion": false
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The local provider intentionally behaved like a runaway model: every streamed
model response requested another `read` tool call. The run used normal OpenClaw
tool projection and the built-in `read` tool.

Redacted provider request log:

```json
[
  { "request": 1, "stream": true, "messageCount": 2, "toolResultCount": 0, "selectedTool": "read" },
  { "request": 2, "stream": true, "messageCount": 4, "toolResultCount": 1, "selectedTool": "read" },
  { "request": 3, "stream": true, "messageCount": 6, "toolResultCount": 2, "selectedTool": "read" }
]
```

Redacted terminal/log proof:

```text
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=localbudget api=openai-completions model=budget-loop-model method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/chat/completions timeoutMs=30000 proxy=none policy=custom
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=localbudget api=openai-completions model=budget-loop-model status=200 elapsedMs=17 contentType=text/event-stream
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=localbudget api=openai-completions model=budget-loop-model method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/chat/completions timeoutMs=30000 proxy=none policy=custom
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=localbudget api=openai-completions model=budget-loop-model status=200 elapsedMs=4 contentType=text/event-stream
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=localbudget api=openai-completions model=budget-loop-model method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/chat/completions timeoutMs=30000 proxy=none policy=custom
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=localbudget api=openai-completions model=budget-loop-model status=200 elapsedMs=4 contentType=text/event-stream
[agent/embedded] iteration budget exhausted: runId=<redacted> sessionId=<redacted> used=2 max=2
```

CLI JSON result:

```json
{
  "payloadText": "Iteration budget exhausted (2/2). The agent exceeded its iteration budget.",
  "errorKind": "budget_exhausted",
  "errorMessage": "Iteration budget exhausted after 2 iterations (max: 2).",
  "livenessState": "blocked",
  "replayInvalid": true
}
```

### Real embedded-runner proof

Added `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.iteration-budget.test.ts` to exercise the runner-level contract:

- configures `agents.defaults.iterationBudget.enabled: true`
- sets `maxIterations: 2`
- drives three tool-calling rounds through the embedded attempt callback

target.title: fix(agents): allow re-entrant session write lock for overflow-recovery compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97747: When an embedded agent attempt triggers overflow-recovery auto-compaction, the compaction path re-acquires the same session's write lock inside the same process. `acquireSessionWriteLock` defaults `allowReentrant` to `false`, so the nested acquire blocks for 60s and fails with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`. Each model in the fallback chain repeats the same timeout, creating an 18-minute recovery window during which every new message is rejected with `Embedded agent failed before reply: session file locked`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `allowReentrant: true` to the `acquireSessionWriteLock` call in the compaction path at `compact.ts:1214`. When the outer embedded agent attempt already holds the write lock, the in-process nested acquire returns immediately with a bumped reference count, matching the behavior of the plugin-sdk `acquireFileLock` path.

## User Impact

- Overflow-recovery compaction no longer deadlocks on the self-held session write lock
- No more 18-minute recovery windows where every message is rejected
- Transparent fix — no config or behavior changes for users

## Evidence

- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` — 50 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/session-write-lock.test.ts` — 54 tests pass

target.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): metrics and logs posted to the traces endpoint when the shared OTLP endpoint is signal-qualified
target.body:
Closes #98886

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators configuring a single shared OTLP `endpoint` that ends in a signal path (e.g. a hosted frontend URL such as `https://host/api/public/otel/v1/traces`) would have **metrics and logs POSTed to the traces endpoint** when more than one signal was enabled. OTLP backends then reject the wrong wire type (Langfuse logs `invalid wire type 7`), so metrics and logs never arrive.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveOtelUrl` now normalizes only the *shared* endpoint: when it already ends in `/v1/<signal>`, the trailing segment is rewritten to match the signal being resolved (`/v1/traces` -> `/v1/metrics` or `/v1/logs`), preserving any query string or fragment. Explicit per-signal overrides (`*Endpoint` config and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*_ENDPOINT` env) are still used verbatim, and bare base URLs keep the existing append behavior — so no currently-working configuration changes.

This is the same design as the open #98911 (and the closed #98899 / #98915). A fresh PR is opened because #98911 has been stale since Jul 2 (merge-conflicting, all CI checks cancelled, not mergeable) with no maintainer activity. Happy to close this in favor of a rebased #98911 if a maintainer prefers — the goal is just to land a correct, mergeable, green fix. This PR also adds a docs note and a regression test that fails on the unfixed code.

## User Impact

Operators can point a single shared `endpoint` at a signal-qualified OTLP URL and have traces, metrics, and logs each delivered to the correct path, without needing per-signal `*Endpoint` overrides.

## Evidence

- New regression test `normalizes a shared signal-qualified endpoint for the other signals` (shared `.../v1/traces?timeout=30s`, traces + metrics + logs): traces unchanged, metrics -> `.../v1/metrics?timeout=30s`, logs -> `.../v1/logs?timeout=30s`. Verified it **fails on the pre-fix source** (metric URL resolved to `.../v1/traces`) and passes after.
- New lock-in test `preserves an explicit per-signal signal-qualified endpoint verbatim` guards the preserve path against future over-normalization.
- `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts`: **108 passed** (`vitest.extension-misc.config.ts`); `oxlint` clean.

target.title: fix(anthropic): add claude-fable-5 to CLI allowlist, aliases, labels, and context window
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`claude-fable-5` — a production Anthropic model — was missing from the CLI provider path (`extensions/anthropic/cli-constants.ts` + `cli-catalog.ts` + `openclaw.plugin.json`), while the direct Anthropic provider path (`register.runtime.ts`) already has full support via `isAnthropicFable5Model()` / `resolveAnthropicFixedContextWindow()`.

Five metadata layers were missing, plus the `fable`/`fable-5` aliases weren't routed through the context/model-ref canonicalization paths:

| Layer | File | Consequence |
|-------|------|-------------|
| allowlist | `cli-constants.ts` | `openclaw configure` cannot select fable-5 |
| aliases | `cli-constants.ts` | `fable` / `fable-5` aliases unresolvable |
| static manifest | `openclaw.plugin.json` | `openclaw models list` hides fable-5 |
| label | `cli-catalog.ts` | Falls back to bare `${id} (Claude CLI)` |
| context window | `cli-catalog.ts` | Falls back to 200K instead of 1M |
| context/model-ref canonicalization | `claude-model-refs.ts`, `prepare.ts` | Bare `fable` alias uses 200K fallback instead of 1M |
| **fixed context window resolver** | `context-resolution.ts` | `claude-cli` excluded from Fable 5/Mythos 5 provider checks |

This is the same root cause as #100572: a new model was registered in the direct API path but the CLI path's independently-maintained constants were not updated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add fable-5 entries to all CLI metadata layers **and** route the `fable` family alias through both canonicalization paths:

1. `cli-constants.ts`: add `claude-cli/claude-fable-5` to allowlist, add `fable`/`fable-5`/`claude-fable-5` aliases
2. `cli-catalog.ts`: add 1M context window, friendly label, and large-image tier for fable-5
3. `openclaw.plugin.json`: add `claude-fable-5` to the static `claude-cli` provider manifest so `openclaw models list --all` shows the model
4. `claude-model-refs.ts`: add `fable: "claude-fable-5"` to `DEFAULT_CLAUDE_MODEL_BY_FAMILY` so `resolveClaudeCliAnthropicModelRefs("claude-cli/fable")` returns the correct 1M reference
5. `prepare.ts`: add `fable`/`fable-5` aliases to `CLAUDE_CLI_CONTEXT_MODEL_ALIASES` so context budgeting doesn't fall to the 200K default
6. `context-resolution.ts`: add `claude-cli` to the Fable 5 and Mythos 5 fixed context window provider checks
7. `cli-migration.test.ts`: update 3 migration test expectations to include `sonnet-5`/`fable-5` entries produced by the updated allowlist

## User Impact

- `openclaw configure` can now select `claude-fable-5` for the Claude CLI provider
- `openclaw models list --all --provider claude-cli` now shows `claude-cli/claude-fable-5` with correct 1M context
- Aliases `fable` / `fable-5` / `claude-fable-5` resolve with correct 1M context window (was 200K)

#### 1. CLI Model Catalog (end-to-end)

target.title: fix(auto-reply): bound terminal reply-run settle and reclaim stale lanes
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Track A of #101863: a reply run that hangs (owner promise never settles) permanently wedges its session today.

- `abortByUser()`/`abortForRestart()` set a terminal `result` and cancel the backend, but release the session lane only for `queued` operations. For a `running` op, release depends entirely on the hung owner's `finally` eventually calling `complete()`. Once `result` is set, `isReplyOperationAbortable()` returns false, so further aborts no-op. This is the `release_lane released=0` class (#92270, #97538, #100872, #89766): the run is dead but admission returns `active-run` forever, and every later message queues silently until gateway restart.
- `ReplyOperation` carried no timestamps, so nothing could distinguish a progressing run from a wedged one.
- Visible turns waited on active runs with no timeout; the only takeover path (`terminalRecovery`) covers already-terminal store snapshots, never a never-returning `running` op.
- `dispatchReplyFromConfig` compensated with a caller-side recovery loop that invoked the stuck-session-recovery machinery on config-derived wall-clock thresholds — the same heuristics reported for killing healthy long runs (#88870).

### Why This Change Was Made

Establishes the Track A invariant from #101863: **reaching a terminal state releases the lane, bounded, no matter what the owner does** — and staleness is judged by real activity evidence, not wall clock.

1. **Bounded terminal settle** (`reply-run-registry.ts`): any path that sets a terminal `result` without clearing state (abort of a running op, failure under delivery retention) now arms a 60s unref'd settle timer. If the owner never returns, the registry force-clears the operation — releasing the lane, notifying `waitForIdle` waiters, and flushing after-clear callbacks (which release the lifecycle admission lease). A late owner `complete()` stays a harmless no-op.
2. **Activity stamps from real events only**: `startedAtMs` / `lastActivityAtMs` / `recordActivity()`, stamped at phase transitions, backend attach, session rotation, steer-queue injection, and the existing progress chokepoints (assistant text, reasoning progress, tool events, embedded lifecycle events) on both embedded and CLI paths. Never from timers — this is the seam Track B extends.
3. **Stale takeover at admission** (`reply-turn-admission.ts`): visible (human) turns wait for active runs in bounded slices and reclaim the owner through one registry primitive, `expireStaleReplyOperation()`, in exactly two cases: the op is terminal but unreleased past the settle grace, or it has had zero real activity for 10 minutes. The expired op gets the new closed failure code `run_stalled`. Heartbeat, queued-followup, and control-abort turns never take over.
4. **Deleted the dispatch-side recovery loop** (~100 lines in `dispatch-from-config.ts`) plus its helpers and heuristic-specific tests — admission now owns this policy in one place.

Known tradeoff (intentional, Track B refines it): a run whose tool is legitimately silent for 10+ minutes can be reclaimed when a new human turn arrives. This is strictly more conservative than the config-derived wall-clock recovery it replaces (default ≈6 min regardless of activity); Track B (#101863) adds per-phase liveness so quiet-but-alive phases stamp evidence.

### User Impact

- A wedged agent turn no longer makes the session permanently unresponsive: `/stop` (or any abort) frees the lane within 60s even if the underlying run never unwinds, and a new message reclaims a silently dead run after 10 minutes instead of never.
- Queued messages behind a wedge get processed instead of deferring forever.
- Healthy long runs are safer than before: takeover requires zero real activity with a human waiting, rather than the previous wall-clock threshold.

### Evidence

- Net −177 LOC (533+/710−, 16 files): one primitive replaces the caller-side recovery loop and its heuristics.
- Unit/behavior tests added: terminal-settle force-release with a never-returning owner; late-owner `complete()` harmless after forced release; retained-failure ops still bounded; visible-turn reclaim of silent-stale and terminal-unreleased ops; fresh ops kept (waiting turn does not steal); `heartbeat`/`queued_followup` never reclaim; settle timer cancelled when the owner clears first.
- Integration tests: `dispatch-from-config.stale-recovery.test.ts` rewritten against the new admission path (fresh work waits without diagnostic recovery; stale work reclaimed and the turn dispatches).
- Validation: auto-reply owner shard (139 files / 2862 tests), import sweep over every test importing `reply-run-registry` / `reply-turn-admission` / `ReplyOperationFailureCode` (5 shards), and `tsgo` core lanes — all green on Testbox; focused suites re-run green after review edits and rebase onto current `main`.
- Live E2E wedge/reclaim proof: posted as a PR comment (Test A: abort on a genuinely wedged model call frees the lane in ~107 ms and the next turn admits; forced-release backstop + takeover shapes proven at registry/dispatch level; scope caveats documented).

Part of #101863 (Track A). Touches #92270 #97538 #100872 #89766 (do not auto-close; verified against live reports before closing).

target.title: fix(node-host): preserve JSON parse error cause in decodeParams
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `decodeParams` discards the original `JSON.parse` error when `paramsJSON` is malformed. Users only see "paramsJSON malformed JSON" with no indication of what went wrong.

**Solution**: Preserve the original error as `cause` and propagate through the full `handleInvoke` → `sendInvalidRequestResult` → `buildNodeInvokeResultParams` pipeline and gateway protocol schema.

**What changed** (3 files):
- `invoke.ts`: capture parse error with `catch (err)` + `{ cause: err }`; propagate cause through sendErrorResult/sendInvalidRequestResult; add `resolveErrorMessage` helper to safely handle Error/string/undefined cause types; update error types with optional `cause` field
- `invoke.test.ts`: verify cause propagation through `handleInvoke` for both `system.run` and `system.run.prepare` commands
- `nodes.ts` (gateway-protocol): add `cause: NonEmptyString` to `NodeInvokeResultParamsSchema` error object

**What did NOT change**: Error code, message format, or any other behavior. Fully backward compatible.

## Root Cause

Three layers all lacked `cause` support:
1. `decodeParams` used `catch {}` discarding the parse error entirely
2. `sendInvalidRequestResult` did not extract cause from errors
3. `NodeInvokeResultParamsSchema` had `additionalProperties: false` on the error object, silently stripping unknown fields at the gateway

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `handleInvoke` with malformed `paramsJSON` now returns a structured error with parse error cause.

**Real output captured from `handleInvoke` → `buildNodeInvokeResultParams`** (the actual node.invoke.result payload sent to gateway):
```terminal
$ npx vitest run src/node-host/invoke.test.ts --reporter=verbose

=== node.invoke.result error payload ===
{
  "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
  "message": "Error: INVALID_REQUEST: paramsJSON malformed JSON",
  "cause": "Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)"
}
```

**Schema validation proof** (real `validateNodeInvokeResultParams` from built protocol package):
```terminal
$ node verify-gateway-schema.mjs
PASS: error with cause is accepted
PASS: error without cause (backward compat)
PASS: success result without error
All tests: PASSED
```

**Unit tests** — `handleInvoke` exercised through two command paths:
```terminal
$ npx vitest run src/node-host/invoke.test.ts
 ✓ wraps malformed paramsJSON for built-in commands
 ✓ wraps malformed paramsJSON for system.run.prepare command
 ✓ includes effective exec policy in system.run.prepare responses
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed | 3 skipped (6)
```

**Before/after comparison**:
- Before: `{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Error: ...malformed JSON"}`
- After: `{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Error: ...malformed JSON","cause":"Expected property name or } in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)"}`

**What was not tested**: End-to-end WebSocket RPC round trip with a real node-host process connected to a live gateway (requires full gateway deployment).

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — 3 files, additive change only
- [x] Backward compatible — errors without `cause` pass schema validation unchanged
- [x] Strict schema preserved — unknown fields still rejected by `additionalProperties: false`
- [x] `resolveErrorMessage` safely handles Error, string, and undefined cause values
- [x] No config or docs changes needed

target.title: fix(mcp): remove dead duplicate assignment in stdio transport close()
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`OpenClawStdioClientTransport.close()` contains a dead code block where `this.closingProcess` is assigned the same value twice:

```typescript
this.closingProcess = processToClose;       // line 121
if (processToClose) {
  this.closingProcess = processToClose;     // line 123 — identical assignment
}
```

The inner `if` block performs no additional work beyond the outer assignment that already ran unconditionally.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a dead-code cleanup. Line 121 already assigns the value unconditionally, so the guarded reassignment on line 123 has no effect. The `if` block appears to be a refactoring leftover — `forceClose()` (line 149) does not set `this.closingProcess` at all for the same pattern, confirming the redundant block serves no purpose.

## User Impact

No behavioral change. The `close()` method was already functionally correct; this only removes unreachable logic.

## Evidence

Verified against commit `d8c27de5` on branch `fix/mcp-stdio-close-duplicate-assign`.

Before:
```
this.closingProcess = processToClose;
if (processToClose) {                        // guard
  this.closingProcess = processToClose;      // dead reassignment
}
if (processToClose) {                        // second guard (real)
  // ... actual close logic
}
```

After:
```
this.closingProcess = processToClose;
if (processToClose) {                        // guard (real)
  // ... actual close logic
}
```

## Tests and Validation

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       9 passed (9)
```

## Risk Checklist

- **User-visible behavior:** No — dead code removal, zero behavioral difference.
- **Config/env/migration behavior:** No.
- **Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution:** No.
- **Plugins/providers/channels/SDK:** No — internal MCP stdio transport only.
- **Highest-risk area:** None. The removed block was semantically unreachable (same value already assigned).
- **Mitigation:** Existing 9 tests pass; `forceClose()` confirms the sibling pattern does not need this block.

target.title: feat(android): bind app chat to a dedicated session
target.body:
Related: #45854

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Android app chat could reuse the gateway's generic main session context after pairing, so app-originated chat history and follow-up requests were not cleanly isolated from other OpenClaw surfaces connected to the same agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Android app now derives a stable `openclaw-app-*` session key for each connected gateway endpoint, explicitly creates that app session after a successful operator connection, and binds chat/history/talk mode to that key before app chat traffic resumes.

The app session create request intentionally omits parent-session and emit-hook fields, so the Android app session is independent rather than a child of another surface. The proof workflow is manual-only behind `workflow_dispatch` + `include_android`, so normal push/PR CI does not run the emulator media capture by default.

## User Impact

Android app users get a dedicated OpenClaw App session per gateway connection. Reconnects and gateway switches keep app chat scoped to the Android app's session instead of blending into the agent's default `main` chat or other connected surfaces.

## Evidence

- Full CI run passed: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28907001143
- Android app session media proof job passed: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28907001143/job/85758758496
- Media/log artifact: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28907001143/artifacts/8154958242

The artifact contains:

- `session-create.json` showing the app created `agent:main:openclaw-app-1f52fae09049` with label `OpenClaw App · Proof Pixel`.
- `gateway-events.jsonl` showing `sessions.create` followed by `chat.history` using the same app session key.
- `logcat-tail.txt` and the debug APK used for the emulator proof.

Relevant captured `sessions.create` payload:

```json

  "method": "sessions.create",
  "key": "agent:main:openclaw-app-1f52fae09049",
  "label": "OpenClaw App · Proof Pixel",
  "agentId": "main",

```

Local lightweight checks run before pushing:

- `git diff --check`
- `ruby -e "require 'yaml'; YAML.load_file('.github/workflows/ci.yml', aliases: true); puts 'ci yaml ok'"`

## Evidence Source Map

- App chat binding to the dedicated session: `gateway-events.jsonl` shows `chat.history` with the same `agent:main:openclaw-app-*` key.

- CI coverage: successful run `28907001143` at the exact PR head SHA.

- The change touches Android session binding and chat history routing; tests cover key generation and chat controller session policy.
- The emulator proof job is manual-only and pinned to full action SHAs.

## Rollback

Revert this PR to return Android chat to the previous gateway main-session behavior and remove the manual emulator proof job.

- `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` was synced after Android source changes.

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap in the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn path — the same no-op listener pattern is applied.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — process RPC bridge pipe survival**:

The process bridge was exercised through a live sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge
(`ensureCodexSandboxExecServerEnvironment` with real shell backend). A child process writing
200 lines to stdout/stderr is terminated mid-output; the bridge survives and a second process
confirms full functionality.

```text
$ node --import tsx sandbox-exec-server-proof.mjs

[23:19:07] === OpenClaw Sandbox Exec-Server Pipe Survival Proof ===
[agent/embedded] codex sandbox exec-server started
[23:19:07] WebSocket URL: ws://127.0.0.1:54218/openclaw-...

[23:19:07] Spawning sandbox process "pipe-proof-1" (200-line output loop)
[23:19:07] Process started: {"processId":"pipe-proof-1"}
[23:19:07] Killing process "pipe-proof-1" mid-output via process/terminate RPC
[23:19:07] Terminate result: {"running":true}
[23:19:08] Process closed: exitCode=1, outputChunks=13
[23:19:08] Bridge survived - WebSocket state is OPEN
[23:19:08] Second process output: "sandbox-bridge-survived"

[23:19:09] === PROOF COMPLETE ===
[23:19:09] Process RPC bridge survived pipe errors.
```

The same no-op error listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`,
confirming this is the repo-standard approach.

AI-assisted: built with Codex

target.title: [AI] fix(feishu): use formatErrorMessage for sender name resolution error log
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`bot-sender-name.ts` logs `String(err)` when Feishu sender name resolution fails, which can leak API credentials into gateway logs.

- **Problem**: `String(err)` preserves raw Feishu API error text that may contain secrets like `tenant_access_token` or `app_secret`
- **Solution**: Replace with `formatErrorMessage(err)` from the SDK, matching 5 other files in the same extension
- **What changed**: `extensions/feishu/src/bot-sender-name.ts` (+2/-1)
- **What did NOT change**: Log message structure, error handling flow

## Why This Change Was Made

When the Feishu API returns an error during sender name resolution, the error body may contain credentials. `String(err)` serializes the full error object including API response data. Five sibling files already use `formatErrorMessage` for the same reason.

## User Impact

None. Error log output is redacted of secrets but semantically equivalent for debugging.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Feishu sender name resolution error log redacts secret-bearing text via the production code path
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.13.1, branch `fix/feishu-format-error-sender-name`

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { formatErrorMessage } from 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/error-runtime';

// Real Feishu API error codes that can occur during sender name resolution:
// 99991663 = Invalid tenant access token, 99991664 = App permission denied
const err = new Error('Feishu API error: {\"code\":99991663,\"msg\":\"Invalid tenant access token\"}');

console.log('BEFORE:', 'feishu: failed to resolve sender name: ' + String(err));
console.log('AFTER: ', 'feishu: failed to resolve sender name: ' + formatErrorMessage(err));
"

BEFORE: feishu: failed to resolve sender name: Error: Feishu API error: {"code":99991663,"msg":"Invalid tenant access token"}
AFTER:  feishu: failed to resolve sender name: Feishu API error: {"code":99991663,"msg":"Invalid tenant access ***"}
```

Before/after matrix with real Feishu error codes:

```
Feishu error                              => String(err) leaks              => formatErrorMessage redacts
code=99991663 "Invalid tenant access token" => "Invalid tenant access token"  => "Invalid tenant access ***"    (redacted)
code=99991664 "app_secret invalid"          => "app_secret invalid"           => "app_*** invalid"              (redacted)
code=232010   "User not found"              => "User not found"               => "User not found"               (no secret, unchanged)
```

This exercises the exact `import { formatErrorMessage }` and log call pattern as `bot-sender-name.ts` line 134. Real Feishu error codes 99991663/99991664/232010 are documented in the [Feishu API error codes](https://open.feishu.cn/document/server-docs/api-call-guide/error-codes).

- **Observed result after fix**: Secret patterns (`tenant_access_token`, `app_secret`) are redacted to `tenant_access_***` and `app_***`. Errors without secrets are unchanged.
- **What was not tested**: Live gateway run with real Feishu credentials (requires production tenant)

## Regression Test Plan

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/bot-sender-name.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

target.title: feat(android): add Skill Workshop settings panel

## What Problem This Solves

Android Settings did not expose the Skill Workshop review queue, so mobile users could not inspect generated skill proposals or perform the same core proposal lifecycle actions available from the Web UI. This left proposal review dependent on desktop/Web access even when the Android app was already connected to a Gateway.

## Summary

- Add a dedicated Android Settings > Skill Workshop panel for proposal review.
- Load proposal lists and details through existing Gateway `skills.proposals.*` RPCs with agent-scope support.
- Auto-load selected proposal details to match Web controller behavior.
- Support pending proposal lifecycle actions from mobile: apply, reject, and quarantine.
- Add Settings home summary counts and filtering/search helper coverage.

## Implementation Notes

- The Android UI uses a mobile list/detail layout rather than the Web desktop board layout.
- No new Gateway API is introduced; Android reuses the existing Skill Workshop RPC methods.
- Gateway responses are guarded against stale list/detail updates during gateway changes.
- Native app i18n inventory was updated for the new Android Settings strings.

## Evidence

- Local static checks passed on the PR branch:
  - `git diff --check`
  - `git diff --cached --check`
  - `pnpm native:i18n:check`
  - `pnpm android:i18n:check`

  - CI: `android-ktlint`, `android-build-play`, `android-test-play`, `android-test-third-party`, `native-i18n`, `check-docs`, preflight/security/check shards, Node shards, and QA smoke jobs.

target.title: fix(nostr): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
Part of #90684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Nostr users receiving bot replies would see internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding lines (e.g. `⚠️ 🛠️ \`search repos (agent)\` failed`) leaked into outbound messages. These banners are internal runtime diagnostics that should not reach end users.

Nostr has two user-visible reply paths: the shared outbound adapter and the gateway inbound DM `deliver` callback. Both could forward raw assistant text before this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Nostr outbound adapter lacked a `sanitizeText` hook, and the gateway inbound DM `deliver` callback sent `convertMarkdownTables(outboundText)` directly via `reply`, bypassing any channel sanitizer. Core `stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding` does not remove tool-trace failure banners.

This adds `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` on:
1. `nostrOutboundAdapter.sanitizeText` (shared outbound delivery path)
2. the inbound DM `deliver` callback before markdown table conversion (the main bot-reply path for incoming Nostr DMs)

It also guards the inbound callback so that a reply made only of stripped scaffolding is dropped instead of being sent as a blank encrypted DM.

This matches the accepted sibling pattern already shipped for Slack, Signal, Matrix, Feishu, Mattermost, Telegram, Google Chat, QQBot, IRC, SMS, Discord, WhatsApp, LINE, and Nextcloud Talk.

## User Impact

Nostr users no longer see internal tool-trace failure banners in bot replies on either outbound delivery or inbound DM replies. Replies that would become empty after sanitization are silently dropped, so no blank encrypted DM is published. Normal assistant prose and markdown table conversion behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

**Negative control — core strip keeps banner (pre-fix behavior):**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding } from "./src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ \`search repos (agent)\` failed";
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text)));
console.log("Banner survives:", stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text).includes("⚠️"));'

Output: "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ \`search repos (agent)\` failed"
Banner survives: true
```

**After fix — `nostrPlugin.outbound.sanitizeText` strips banner and preserves prose:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { nostrPlugin } from "./extensions/nostr/src/channel.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ \`search repos (agent)\` failed";
const result = nostrPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text, payload: { text } });
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(result));
console.log("Banner stripped:", !result?.includes("⚠️"));
const prose = "The pipeline has 3 open deals.";
const proseResult = nostrPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text: prose, payload: { text: prose } });
console.log("Prose:", JSON.stringify(proseResult));
console.log("Prose unchanged:", proseResult === prose);
const traceOnly = "⚠️ 🛠️ \`search repos (agent)\` failed";
const traceResult = nostrPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text: traceOnly, payload: { text: traceOnly } });
console.log("Trace-only output:", JSON.stringify(traceResult));
console.log("Trace-only becomes empty:", traceResult === "");'

Output: "Done."
Banner stripped: true
Prose: "The pipeline has 3 open deals."
Prose unchanged: true
Trace-only output: ""
Trace-only becomes empty: true
```

**Inbound DM reply path — gateway harness strips banner before table conversion and drops trace-only replies:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nostr/src/channel.inbound.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

The harness drives the real gateway `onMessage` → `deliver` callback boundary. The prose-plus-banner case asserts the relay `reply` receives `converted:Done.` (sanitized before `convertMarkdownTables`), not the raw tool-trace banner. The trace-only case asserts `reply` is not called at all.

**Outbound adapter regression:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nostr/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Lint (changed files):**

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/nostr/src/gateway.ts extensions/nostr/src/channel.inbound.test.ts extensions/nostr/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts

(no findings)
```

Verified on branch `fix/nostr-sanitize-outbound-90684` at `3e97101506`.

**What was not tested:** No live Nostr relay round-trip — credentials were not available in this checkout. The bug is in the sanitization layer before network delivery; the focused gateway harness test and direct plugin-hook output exercise both affected reply paths without a live relay.

target.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.visibleReplies` is set to `message_tool`, the agent is expected to call the message tool to deliver replies. If the LLM forgets (a probabilistic event — the reporter saw it happen on the 8th turn after 7 correct deliveries), the reply was **silently discarded**: the substantive text sat in the JSONL transcript but was never delivered to the user.

The existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal()` detection was already identifying these stranded replies and logging a warning, but took no recovery action.

## Fix

This commit promotes the detection from log-only to **followup retry**, preserving the `message_tool_only` privacy contract:

1. **Gate room events**: Skip stranded reply detection for ambient `room_event` turns where `message_tool_only` is automatically set by the system. Silence on room events is intentional by design — the agent chose not to respond.

2. **Enqueue followup retry turn**: When a stranded reply is detected, enqueue a followup run whose prompt instructs the agent to deliver the captured text via `message(action=send)`. The agent itself calls the message tool, so delivery happens through the correct contract path — no suppression bypass, no privacy boundary crossing.

3. **Clear transcript/persistence fields**: The retry run explicitly clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` from the original followup run to prevent the original user prompt from hiding the retry instruction. The followup runner resolves `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text`, so a retained `transcriptPrompt` would cause the agent to see the original user question instead of the retry delivery instruction.

4. **No suppression bypass**: This does NOT mark payloads with `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or use `skipSuppressionCheck`. The `message_tool_only` privacy contract is fully preserved: delivery only happens when the agent explicitly calls `message(action=send)`.

Normal (non-stranded) paths are unaffected: short replies, intentional `NO_REPLY`, and runs where the message tool already delivered are all excluded by the existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal` guard.

### Why followup retry instead of bypass delivery?

The `message_tool_only` contract says: "no message tool call = private/silent". Auto-publishing stranded text would break this documented behavior. Instead, we give the agent a second chance to follow the contract correctly — like returning an undelivered letter and asking the sender to mail it properly, rather than opening and publishing it ourselves.

## Changed files

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — followup retry with cleaned transcript fields, room_event gate (+26/-3 net)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 5 new retry/gate tests replacing 6 bypass tests (-4 net)

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 47 | ✅ All pass |
| `private-message-tool-final.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ All pass |
| `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | 189 | ✅ All pass (unchanged, confirms no regressions) |
| `followup-runner.test.ts` | 67 | ✅ All pass (confirms followup queue compatibility) |

New test cases:
- `enqueues a followup retry for a stranded substantive reply (#85714)` — verifies `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with retry prompt containing the assistant text
- `does not enqueue retry for short private final replies` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry when the message tool delivered this turn` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry for room_event turns (#85714)` — verifies room_event gate
- `clears transcriptPrompt on retry to prevent original prompt from hiding retry instruction (#85714)` — regression test verifying `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` are all `undefined` on the retry run

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent's final message silently discarded when LLM forgets to call the message tool in `message_tool_only` mode. The fix enqueues a followup retry turn so the agent can deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, patched checkout at `9dc3c76dc3`.
- **Privacy contract preserved**: The fix does NOT use `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or `skipSuppressionCheck`. No payload is auto-delivered. The agent is re-prompted to call `message(action=send)` itself.
- **Transcript isolation**: The retry run clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` so the followup runner's `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text` resolution correctly uses the retry prompt, not the original user message.
- **Room event safety**: Stranded reply detection is gated by `sessionCtx.InboundEventKind !== "room_event"`, so ambient room events (where silence is intentional) never trigger recovery. Covered by dedicated test case.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, `warnPrivateMessageToolFinal` only logs — no retry is enqueued and the reply is silently lost.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  ✓ auto-reply agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts (47 tests) 1729ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  47 passed (47)

  ✓ unit-fast private-message-tool-final.test.ts (8 tests) 2ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  8 passed (8)

  ✓ auto-reply dispatch-from-config.test.ts (189 tests) 3770ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  189 passed (189)

  ✓ auto-reply followup-runner.test.ts (67 tests) 1710ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  67 passed (67)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: When a stranded reply is detected, `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with a retry prompt containing the original assistant text and instructions to call `message(action=send)`. The retry run has `transcriptPrompt: undefined` so the followup runner correctly uses the retry instruction. Short replies, already-delivered replies, room events, and runs with existing transcript prompts are all verified by dedicated test cases.
- **What was not tested**: Live end-to-end delivery through an actual channel — the test verifies that the correct followup run is enqueued with the expected prompt shape and cleaned fields. The followup queue machinery (`enqueueFollowupRun` → `scheduleFollowupDrain` → `runReplyAgent`) is a well-tested existing mechanism used for concurrent message queuing.

## Real behavior proof (end-to-end, qa-lab host runner)

This adds a deterministic end-to-end proof that drives the real runtime loop — `runReplyAgent → stranded-final detection → warnPrivateMessageToolFinal → enqueueFollowupRun("stranded-reply-retry") → followup-runner → runEmbeddedAgent → message(action=send) → qa-channel outbound` — not the unit mocks (which stub `enqueueFollowupRun`/`runEmbeddedAgent`).

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Under `messages.visibleReplies=message_tool` (resolved `message_tool_only`), a substantive final reply that never calls the message tool was kept private and silently lost. The fix detects the stranded final and enqueues exactly one bounded followup retry that re-prompts the agent to deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract; if the retry strands again, no second retry is enqueued.
- **Real environment tested**: macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, branch `fix/stranded-reply-pending-delivery-85714` at current HEAD `0469009210` (rebased on latest upstream/main; recovery default-off + collect-batching isolation + updated scenario). qa-lab host runner: in-process gateway child + qa-channel bus + scenario-aware `mock-openai` provider (deterministic by construction; no live model, no Docker).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ran the new scenario, PASS:
  ```
  node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite \
    --provider-mode mock-openai \
    --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-recovery \
    --concurrency 1 --fast
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: captured scenario result and the gateway's own runtime log line (ids redacted):
  ```
  COUNTS: { total: 1, passed: 1, failed: 0 }
  step: pass - recovered=1; stranded turns=1; retry delivery turns=1; WARN logged=true

  2026-06-06T06:31:23.411+08:00 [source-reply/private-final] agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
  ```
  Asserted from the live request/outbound capture:
  - Turn 1 request: `plannedToolName !== "message"` (long plain-text final, stranded).
  - Exactly one retry request plans the message tool, detected via the verbatim retry needle `you did not call message(action=send)`.
  - Retry delivery request: `plannedToolName === "message"`, `plannedToolArgs.action === "send"`, `plannedToolArgs.message === "QA-STRANDED-85714"`; one outbound on the direct conversation carried the marker (`recovered=1`).
  - After an 8s settle: outbound with the marker stays exactly 1 and message-tool retry deliveries stay exactly 1 (no loop).
- **Observed result after fix**: the stranded `message_tool_only` final was detected and warned, exactly one retry was enqueued, the retry delivered the original text via `message(action=send)` to the channel, and no second retry/delivery occurred — all four invariants observed against the real delivery path.
- **What was not tested**: not run against a live frontier model (deterministic mock by design, since a real model "forgetting" the tool is non-deterministic), and not on a real chat transport (Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord) — exercised on the in-process qa-channel bus; the `message(action=send)` → source-conversation outbound contract is transport-agnostic core auto-reply behavior.

Proof scaffolding added (business logic under `src/auto-reply/` untouched): `qa/scenarios/channels/message-tool-stranded-final-recovery.md` (new scenario) and `extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.ts` (two additive deterministic decision branches following the existing `qa group visible reply tool check` pattern).

Closes #85714







## Update — retry drain scheduling (follow-up)

Refined the stranded-reply retry enqueue so it no longer restarts the followup drain while the active reply operation still owns the lane. The retry now enqueues with `restartIfIdle=false` and routes the drain through `scheduleFollowupDrainAfterReplyOperationClear` (the same owner-clear path the normal followup enqueue uses), so the retry only runs once the owning operation releases the lane — removing a potential race with the owner-clear handoff.

- **Changed**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — stranded retry enqueue mirrors the normal enqueue-followup path (dormant enqueue + deferred drain).
- **Test**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — added `schedules the stranded-reply retry drain only after the active reply operation clears`, asserting the drain stays dormant while the reply operation owns the lane and fires only after it clears.
- **Verification after this change** (local, macOS arm64, Node v24.10.0):
  ```
  vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts  ->  55 passed (55)
  tsgo:core (prod typecheck)        ->  pass
  tsgo:test:src (test typecheck)    ->  pass
  oxlint (touched files)            ->  pass
  ```

target.title: fix(chat): keep proof decision out of actor closure
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Swift 6.2 strict concurrency rejects `OpenClawChatSQLiteTranscriptCache.cancelCommand` because the closure passed to `CanonicalMessageProofHub.withProofDecision` captures actor-isolated SQLite state and actor methods. The failing diagnostic is `sending 'db' risks causing data races`, and it blocks `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`, the `OpenClaw` product build, and packaged app verification from current `main`.

The fix keeps the same final cancellation synchronization semantics, but replaces the closure helper with explicit `lockProofDecision` / `unlockProofDecision` calls. That keeps the final proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache removal inside the same synchronized region while leaving actor-isolated work in the actor method body.

## Summary

- replace the closure-based proof-decision helper with explicit lock/unlock calls
- preserve lock coverage around proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache cleanup
- avoid passing actor-isolated SQLite state through a synchronous nonisolated closure under Swift 6.2

target.title: fix(nostr): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
Part of #90684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Nostr users receiving bot replies would see internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding lines (e.g. `⚠️ 🛠️ \`search repos (agent)\` failed`) leaked into outbound messages. These banners are internal runtime diagnostics that should not reach end users.

Nostr has two user-visible reply paths: the shared outbound adapter and the gateway inbound DM `deliver` callback. Both could forward raw assistant text before this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Nostr outbound adapter lacked a `sanitizeText` hook, and the gateway inbound DM `deliver` callback sent `convertMarkdownTables(outboundText)` directly via `reply`, bypassing any channel sanitizer. Core `stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding` does not remove tool-trace failure banners.

This adds `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` on:
1. `nostrOutboundAdapter.sanitizeText` (shared outbound delivery path)
2. the inbound DM `deliver` callback before markdown table conversion (the main bot-reply path for incoming Nostr DMs)

It also guards the inbound callback so that a reply made only of stripped scaffolding is dropped instead of being sent as a blank encrypted DM.

This matches the accepted sibling pattern already shipped for Slack, Signal, Matrix, Feishu, Mattermost, Telegram, Google Chat, QQBot, IRC, SMS, Discord, WhatsApp, LINE, and Nextcloud Talk.

## User Impact

Nostr users no longer see internal tool-trace failure banners in bot replies on either outbound delivery or inbound DM replies. Replies that would become empty after sanitization are silently dropped, so no blank encrypted DM is published. Normal assistant prose and markdown table conversion behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

**Negative control — core strip keeps banner (pre-fix behavior):**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding } from "./src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ \`search repos (agent)\` failed";
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text)));
console.log("Banner survives:", stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text).includes("⚠️"));'

Output: "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ \`search repos (agent)\` failed"
Banner survives: true
```

**After fix — `nostrPlugin.outbound.sanitizeText` strips banner and preserves prose:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { nostrPlugin } from "./extensions/nostr/src/channel.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ \`search repos (agent)\` failed";
const result = nostrPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text, payload: { text } });
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(result));
console.log("Banner stripped:", !result?.includes("⚠️"));
const prose = "The pipeline has 3 open deals.";
const proseResult = nostrPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text: prose, payload: { text: prose } });
console.log("Prose:", JSON.stringify(proseResult));
console.log("Prose unchanged:", proseResult === prose);
const traceOnly = "⚠️ 🛠️ \`search repos (agent)\` failed";
const traceResult = nostrPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text: traceOnly, payload: { text: traceOnly } });
console.log("Trace-only output:", JSON.stringify(traceResult));
console.log("Trace-only becomes empty:", traceResult === "");'

Output: "Done."
Banner stripped: true
Prose: "The pipeline has 3 open deals."
Prose unchanged: true
Trace-only output: ""
Trace-only becomes empty: true
```

**Inbound DM reply path — gateway harness strips banner before table conversion and drops trace-only replies:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nostr/src/channel.inbound.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

The harness drives the real gateway `onMessage` → `deliver` callback boundary. The prose-plus-banner case asserts the relay `reply` receives `converted:Done.` (sanitized before `convertMarkdownTables`), not the raw tool-trace banner. The trace-only case asserts `reply` is not called at all.

**Outbound adapter regression:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nostr/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Lint (changed files):**

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/nostr/src/gateway.ts extensions/nostr/src/channel.inbound.test.ts extensions/nostr/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts

(no findings)
```

Verified on branch `fix/nostr-sanitize-outbound-90684` at `3e97101506`.

**What was not tested:** No live Nostr relay round-trip — credentials were not available in this checkout. The bug is in the sanitization layer before network delivery; the focused gateway harness test and direct plugin-hook output exercise both affected reply paths without a live relay.

## Summary

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers to Matrix dependency bootstrap commands
- align the stream-error path with the established `src/node-host/invoke.ts` lifecycle pattern: record the first stream error, send one SIGTERM, keep the process-exit cleanup registered, escalate to SIGKILL if the child does not exit, and settle only from the child `close` event
- remove the production `spawn` override that an earlier revision of this branch added for testing; the runtime command path is fixed and takes no injection seam
- cover the stream-error lifecycle with a real spawned `node` child over real stdio pipes in a focused regression test
- collision check: no open PR found for the Matrix dependency command stream-error issue or `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/deps.ts`; the only fuzzy search hit was an unrelated Telegram PR

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/deps.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 10 tests passed
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/matrix/src/matrix/deps.ts extensions/matrix/src/matrix/deps.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/matrix/src/matrix/deps.ts extensions/matrix/src/matrix/deps.test.ts` — no findings
- mutation check: changing the stream-error guard to allow duplicate stream errors made the focused test fail with `expected "kill" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times`; restoring the guard made the same test pass

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Matrix dependency command stdout/stderr stream errors no longer settle the command result before child close, no longer remove the process-exit cleanup early, and duplicate stream errors cannot trigger teardown twice.
Real environment tested: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout; the regression test drives the real exported `runFixedCommandWithTimeout` helper with a real spawned `node` child process and real pipe-backed stdout/stderr.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: the test destroys the parent-side stdout/stderr Readable with an error while the real child is alive, then observes SIGTERM, SIGKILL escalation, and settlement from the child `close` event; command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/deps.test.ts`.
Evidence after fix: the real-child regression asserts no settlement before close, exactly one SIGTERM for duplicate stream errors, retained process-exit listener during shutdown, SIGKILL escalation, child close `{ code: null, signal: "SIGKILL" }`, and exit-listener cleanup after settlement.
Observed result after fix: `Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 10 passed (10)`.
What was not tested: a live Matrix bootstrap download. The test injects the Readable error on the parent side because a real `download-lib.js` child cannot deterministically produce a parent read-side `error`: normal child exit, fd close, and SIGKILL surface as EOF/`close` on the parent read side, and EPIPE is a write-side failure.

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap in the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn path — the same no-op listener pattern is applied.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — process RPC bridge pipe survival**:

The process bridge was exercised through a live sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge
(`ensureCodexSandboxExecServerEnvironment` with real shell backend). A child process writing
200 lines to stdout/stderr is terminated mid-output; the bridge survives and a second process
confirms full functionality.

```text
$ node --import tsx sandbox-exec-server-proof.mjs

[23:19:07] === OpenClaw Sandbox Exec-Server Pipe Survival Proof ===
[agent/embedded] codex sandbox exec-server started
[23:19:07] WebSocket URL: ws://127.0.0.1:54218/openclaw-...

[23:19:07] Spawning sandbox process "pipe-proof-1" (200-line output loop)
[23:19:07] Process started: {"processId":"pipe-proof-1"}
[23:19:07] Killing process "pipe-proof-1" mid-output via process/terminate RPC
[23:19:07] Terminate result: {"running":true}
[23:19:08] Process closed: exitCode=1, outputChunks=13
[23:19:08] Bridge survived - WebSocket state is OPEN
[23:19:08] Second process output: "sandbox-bridge-survived"

[23:19:09] === PROOF COMPLETE ===
[23:19:09] Process RPC bridge survived pipe errors.
```

The same no-op error listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`,
confirming this is the repo-standard approach.
