target.title: fix(signal): complete bidirectional quote-reply support
target.body:
## Summary

Adds complete bidirectional Signal quote-reply support — both outbound (agent → user) and inbound (user → agent) quote context handling.

## Problem

**Outbound (agent → user):** When the assistant includes reply tags (`[[reply_to_current]]`, `[[reply_to:<id>]]`), they were stripped but never translated into signal-cli quote parameters. Signal showed no visual reply indicator, unlike Discord/Telegram/Slack.

**Inbound (user → agent):** When a user quote-replies to the agent, the quoted message context was either lost or only used as fallback body text. The agent had no structured awareness of what was being quoted, who wrote it, or that a quote-reply was even happening.

## Solution

### Outbound Changes (agent → user)

1. **Signal outbound adapter** (`src/channels/plugins/outbound/signal.ts`)
   - Updated `sendText()` and `sendMedia()` to pass `replyToId` and `quoteAuthor`

2. **Signal send function** (`src/signal/send.ts`)
   - Added `replyTo` and `quoteAuthor` to `SignalSendOpts`
   - Converts `replyTo` timestamp into signal-cli `quote-timestamp` / `quote-author` RPC params
   - Uses `Number()` instead of `parseInt()` for strict timestamp validation
   - Guards group quotes: skips quoting when `quoteAuthor` is missing (avoids silent signal-cli failures)

3. **Delivery layer** (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts`)
   - `trackReplyConsumption` pattern for bestEffort partial-failure handling
   - `sendPayload` branch routes through quote gating
   - Reply metadata consumed only after successful send
   - Per-payload explicit `replyToId` preserved independently of inherited reply

4. **Event handler — outbound** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.ts`)
   - `resolveQuotedAuthor()` with LRU cache for group quote-author resolution
   - Only falls back to current sender for `[[reply_to_current]]`, not explicit `[[reply_to:<id>]]`

### Inbound Changes (user → agent)

5. **Expanded quote types** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.types.ts`)
   - `SignalQuote` type captures full signal-cli payload: `id`, `author`, `authorNumber`, `authorUuid`, `text`, `mentions`, `attachments`, `textStyles`
   - New `SignalQuotedAttachment`, `SignalTextStyle`, `SignalReplyTarget` types

6. **Quote context module** (`src/signal/monitor/quote-context.ts` — NEW)
   - `describeSignalReplyTarget()` extracts structured quote context from inbound messages
   - `normalizeSignalQuoteId()` validates quote timestamps with strict `Number()` parsing
   - Author resolution cascade: `authorNumber` → `authorUuid` → `author` → LRU cache fallback
   - Handles mentions in quoted text, media attachment placeholders, edge cases

7. **Structured context surfacing** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.ts`)
   - Inbound quotes surfaced as `ReplyToId`, `ReplyToBody`, `ReplyToSender`, `ReplyToIsQuote`
   - Both the user message AND the quoted text are preserved
   - Group and DM quote handling unified

### Tests

- Comprehensive test suite for outbound quote mechanics
- New `event-handler.inbound-contract.test.ts` for inbound quote contract tests
- Refactored `event-handler.quote.test.ts` with edge case coverage
- All tests passing

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Outbound Signal quote-reply parameters were never translated into signal-cli `quote-timestamp` / `quote-author` RPC params, and inbound user quote-replies were dropped or only surfaced as fallback body text. After this fix, `resolveSignalQuoteMetadata` produces the right RPC param shape (and gates out unsafe group quotes), and `describeSignalReplyTarget` returns a structured `SignalReplyTarget` with normalized id, resolved author, body text or media placeholder, and quote kind.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at HEAD `e3740e0223dba46315f0f568d68a14e4ac72fe59` of branch `fix/signal-quote-reply`. Linux 6.12.67, Node v24.15.0, pnpm-driven monorepo. Patched modules in `extensions/signal/src/reply-quote.ts` and `extensions/signal/src/monitor/quote-context.ts` loaded directly with `tsx` from the working tree, and the built CLI (`pnpm openclaw --version`) reports `OpenClaw 2026.5.4 (e3740e0)` confirming the binary is built from the patched commit.

target.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier
target.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: tiered bootstrap loading — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) controls which workspace files are injected into each session's context window. Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

target.title: fix(memory-core): guard supplement lookup in resolveMemoryReadFailureResult with try-catch (fixes #101809)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `memory_get corpus=all` primary read fails, the tool calls `resolveMemoryReadFailureResult` which attempts supplement lookup via `getSupplementMemoryReadResult()`. If the supplement lookup throws (e.g., config loading or database issue), the error propagates as an unhandled rejection because:

1. `resolveMemoryReadFailureResult` is **already inside the outer `catch` block** of `executeMemoryReadResult`
2. The supplement call inside it **has no try-catch guard**
3. The error escapes as an unhandled rejection instead of returning the structured `{disabled: true}` error result

Fixes #101809.

## Changes

### `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts`

Wrap the supplement lookup call in `resolveMemoryReadFailureResult` with try-catch. When supplement lookup fails, fall through to return the original primary memory-read structured error (`{path, text: "", disabled: true, error: "..."}`) instead of crashing.

### `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts`

Add proof test `"returns structured error when supplement lookup throws in memory_get corpus=all fallback"`:
1. Primary memory read throws
2. Registered corpus supplement `get()` throws
3. Asserts the result is the **original primary disabled result** (`error` contains "primary read failed", does NOT contain "supplement lookup failed")

## Evidence

target.title: fix(feishu): accumulate streamed final delta chunks (#91562)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #91562 — Feishu streaming replies only showed the **latest token** (`你` / `好` / `啊`) instead of progressively accumulating text (`你` / `你好` / `你好啊`) in 6.1.

The regression lives in the Feishu streaming-card reply dispatcher. When a reply is streamed and a `final` payload arrives, the handler **overwrote** the accumulated buffer with the latest payload:

```ts
if (info?.kind === "final") {
  streamText = text;            // ← replaces, dropping everything streamed so far
  ...
}
```

When a runtime delivers the reply as a *sequence of incremental `final` chunks* — which DeepSeek streaming (`deepseek-v4-flash`) does — each chunk replaced the buffer, so only the last fragment survived on the card.

## Root cause

`extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts` accumulates streamed text into `streamText`. Two of the three streaming paths already accumulate correctly:

| Path | Handling | Behaviour |
|------|----------|-----------|
| `onPartialReply` (snapshot) | `mergeStreamingText` | ✅ accumulates |
| `block` delivery (delta) | `streamText = `…`${nextText}`` (append) | ✅ accumulates |
| **`final` delivery** | **`streamText = text` (replace)** | ❌ **drops prior tokens** |

The `final` branch was the only place that *assigned* instead of *appending/merging*. A plain assignment is correct when a `final` carries the complete reply, but it loses data when finals arrive incrementally (or when a trailing final only carries the last delta, downgrading an otherwise-correct accumulated preview).

## Before / After

Streamed preview as observed on the card (reproduced in the dispatcher test harness):

| Step | Before (buggy) | After (fixed) |
|------|----------------|---------------|
| chunk `你` | `你` | `你` |
| chunk `好` | `好` | `你好` |
| chunk `啊` | `啊` | `你好啊` |
| **card close** | **`啊`** | **`你好啊`** |

## Minimal repro

With Feishu streaming enabled and a runtime that streams `final` chunks:

```ts
await deliver({ text: "你" }, { kind: "final" });
await deliver({ text: "好" }, { kind: "final" });
await deliver({ text: "啊" }, { kind: "final" });
// before: card shows 啊
// after:  card shows 你好啊
```

## Fix

Introduce `mergeFinalStreamingText` (next to the existing `mergeStreamingText` in `streaming-card.ts`) and use it in the `final` branch:

- **Cumulative re-render / extension** (`next` contains/extends the buffer) → take the fuller text (preserves the existing "coalesce distinct final payloads" behaviour).
- **Final restates a buffered fragment** (buffer contains `next`) → keep the longer accumulation (a trailing delta can no longer downgrade the preview).
- **No containment** → a complete re-render restates the reply from the start and shares a leading run with the buffer, so it *replaces*; an incremental token delta continues from the end and shares no prefix, so it is *appended*.

This keeps replace semantics for genuine complete re-renders while accumulating incremental deltas, so no text is lost.

## Architecture note

The fix is intentionally contained to the Feishu channel's streaming-card buffer, where the symptom surfaces, rather than the provider/transport layer. Channels own how streamed text is rendered into their native surface (Feishu Card Kit updates here), and the dispatcher already maintains a single `streamText` accumulation buffer shared by the partial-snapshot, block-delta, and final paths. Making the `final` path merge into that buffer — instead of clobbering it — brings it in line with the other two paths and makes the buffer resilient to any runtime that chooses to stream finals incrementally, regardless of the upstream provider. The merge helper is pure and unit-tested, mirroring `mergeStreamingText`.

## Tests

Added 7 tests (fail without the fix, pass with it):

- `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts`
  - accumulates incremental `final` delta chunks into the streaming card (#91562)
  - keeps accumulated streaming text when a trailing `final` delta arrives (#91562)
  - replaces the streamed preview with a cumulative `final` extension (guard)
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts` — unit coverage for `mergeFinalStreamingText` (append deltas, keep buffer on restated fragment, prefer cumulative extension, replace on complete re-render, empty-input no-ops)

```
extension-feishu: 69 files, 905 tests passed
oxlint: clean · oxfmt: clean · tsgo (extensions): clean
```

The existing **"coalesces distinct final payloads into one streaming card until idle"** test continues to pass unchanged.

> **Note for maintainers:** I left `CHANGELOG.md` untouched since it appears to be curated at release time (with the attribution linter). Happy to add an entry under the appropriate train if you'd like.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Real behavior proof

I'm an external contributor without access to a live Feishu tenant + DeepSeek (`deepseek-v4-flash`) streaming deployment, so I can't attach a Feishu screen recording. The closest direct evidence I can provide is **console output from executing the real shipped function** (`mergeFinalStreamingText`) over the exact token sequence from the issue, plus the buggy `streamText = text` path for contrast:

```
$ # runtime streams the reply as incremental `final` chunks: 你 / 好 / 啊

BEFORE fix (streamText = text):                  card updates = ["你","好","啊"]      ; final card = "啊"
AFTER  fix (mergeFinalStreamingText):            card updates = ["你","你好","你好啊"] ; final card = "你好啊"
AFTER  fix (trailing delta after good preview):  card updates = ["你好啊"]            ; final card = "你好啊"
```

This reproduces the issue's reported symptom exactly (`你 / 好 / 啊` → only `啊`) and shows the fixed accumulation (`你 / 你好 / 你好啊`). The same behaviour is asserted end-to-end through the real reply dispatcher in `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` (the harness only stubs the Card Kit HTTP calls; the accumulation logic under test is the real code).

🙏 **Maintainer override request:** could a maintainer apply the `proof:` override? A genuine end-to-end Feishu Card Kit capture needs a Feishu app + a DeepSeek streaming account that aren't available to an external contributor, and I'd rather request the override than attach fabricated "live" evidence. Happy to coordinate if there's a sanctioned way to capture real-setup output.

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency.

Related: #97638

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled:

1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace.
2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts.
3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `<location>` paths). Skill names are XML-escaped. The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides.
4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution.

## User Impact

```json5
{
  agents: { defaults: { sandbox: {
    skipSkillsSync: true,
    docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" }
  } } }
}
```

Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (Docker container)

## What Problem This Solves When a user quote-replies to the bot's message in a Microsoft Teams 1:1 DM, the bot could not see the quoted message content — it only saw the user's new text. Root cause: Teams delivers the quoted text of a quote-reply inside `

…

` (a truncated snippet), but `extractMSTeamsQuoteInfo` only matched `

…

`. The match failed, `quoteInfo` came back `undefined`, and nothing was surfaced to the agent via `supplemental.quote`. ## Why This Change Was Made 1. **Parser (primary):** `extractMSTeamsQuoteInfo` now matches `

` **or** `

` (prefers `copy`, falls back to `preview`) and captures the blockquote `itemid` as the quoted message id. 2. **Full text via Graph (enhancement):** the `preview` snippet is Teams-truncated, so when the quoted message id is known and the conversation is a **1:1 DM**, fetch the complete text via the app-only endpoint `GET /chats/{chatId}/messages/{id}` (`Chat.Read.All`) and use it as the quote body. Any failure degrades to the truncated preview, so message handling never breaks. ## User Impact Teams users who quote-reply the bot in a 1:1 DM now get responses that account for the quoted message instead of ignoring it. Group and channel quote replies surface the previously-dropped preview snippet. No configuration changes; no impact on non-quote messages. ## Evidence **Parser, against the exact Teams quote-reply payload** (redacted): ``` BEFORE (copy-only regex): undefined -> quote dropped AFTER (fixed parser): { sender: "", body: "San Francisco right now ... 54-64 °F (avg…)", id: "1783379480258" } ``` **Live in a real Teams tenant** (1:1 DM; redacted screenshots shared with reviewers, kept as external artifacts rather than committed): the bot now reads back the full quoted message instead of only the new text. Also deployed live on a production Teams gateway (`@openclaw/msteams` 2026.6.6): the gateway restarted clean (`[msteams] starting provider`) and a real quote-reply surfaces the quoted body to the agent. **Validation:** msteams suites 85 passing (incl. a group-chat gate regression test); `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` clean. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where repeated failed `exec` calls would never trigger the
no-progress circuit breaker when the error output text varied across calls.
This happens commonly with SSH timeouts, Docker connection-refused errors, and
other transient failures where timestamps or session ids in the error message
change each time while the actual failure mode is identical.

Fixes #93917

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts:196-246` | Split `hashExecToolOutcome`: `completed` keeps output; `failed` strips volatile text but preserves `{status,exitCode,timedOut,failureKind,exitSignal}` with numeric signal normalization via `normalizeExitSignal()` |
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts:670-806` | Restore `date` test (warning), upgrade `flaky-helper` (critical/breaker), add `distinct failure kinds` + `distinct exitSignal values` tests |
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts` | **Runtime proof** — direct tsx execution through production code path (no vitest mocks), shows subsystem logger output |

## Why This Change Was Made

Split `hashExecToolOutcome` so `failed` exec results are hashed without the
volatile output text, while `completed` exec results keep output in the hash
as a real progress signal. A failed command producing different error strings
across identical retries should still count as no-progress.

## User Impact

Stuck agents that loop retrying the same failed `exec` call now correctly hit
the global circuit breaker after the configured threshold, stopping runaway
sessions instead of burning tokens forever.

## Evidence

### Runtime proof (direct Node.js, no vitest)

`src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts` exercises the fix through the
**production `detectToolCallLoop` code path** using `tsx` — no vitest, no mocks.
The test bypasses vitest's module isolation and verifies the real subsystem
logger output.

**Real environment:**
- OS: Linux x86_64, kernel 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node.js v24.13.1, tsx v4.22.3
- Commit: `204c3bd9`

**Exact command:**

```
$ /path/to/tsx src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts
```

**Full terminal output:**

```
=== Real runtime proof: failed-exec loop detection (#93917) ===

Prove 1: Repeated docker-ps failures (same failureKind, varying error text)
[agents/loop-detection] Global circuit breaker triggered: exec repeated 30 times with no progress
  stuck=true  level=critical  detector=global_circuit_breaker
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — circuit breaker triggered

Prove 2: Repeated date calls (completed, varying output)
[agents/loop-detection] Loop warning: exec called 30 times with identical arguments
  stuck=true  level=warning  detector=generic_repeat
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — varying completed output stays at warning

Prove 3: Mixed failure kinds (timeout/terminated/connection_refused)
[agents/loop-detection] Loop warning: exec called 30 times with identical arguments
  stuck=true  level=warning  detector=generic_repeat
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — distinct failure modes not merged

Prove 4: Numeric exitSignal (9=SIGKILL) vs string (SIGTERM)
[agents/loop-detection] Loop warning: exec called 30 times with identical arguments
  stuck=true  level=warning  detector=generic_repeat
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — numeric and string exitSignals kept distinct

=== All runtime proofs complete ===
```

**Observed result after fix:**
- Failed exec with same failureKind + exitCode now fires `global_circuit_breaker` ✅
- Completed exec with varying output stays at `warning` (output IS progress) ✅
- Different failureKind values produce distinct hashes — no false merge ✅
- Numeric exitSignal (9) and string exitSignal ("SIGTERM") produce distinct hashes ✅
- The `[agents/loop-detection]` subsystem logger confirms real production code path

### Unit tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  61 passed (61)
```

**What was not tested:** Live gateway integration with real `exec` tool calls — the
change is pure hash computation; coverage for non-exec tool types is unchanged.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes #101909.

The reply-session initializer's conflict branch in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` allowed a single stale-snapshot retry and then threw `reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`. Because initialization never completed, the session-store entry was never committed and the session wedged **permanently** for that `sessionKey`: every subsequent turn re-hit the same conflict, completed tool executions (`exec`/`read`/etc.) had no channel back to the model, and tool-results silently returned empty. It survived gateway restarts (the conflict is keyed to the persistent sessionKey) and cleared only on a fresh session.

This is **runtime-agnostic** and was observed on both the native (Anthropic) runtime and the Codex app-server harness. On the Codex harness the never-written transcript mirror (`<session>.jsonl.codex-app-server.json`, which carries the threadId) is the runtime-specific casualty, but the root cause is the conflict branch failing to recover.

## Fix
The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks (a runtime-agnostic fan-out where each runtime releases its lane and clears its stale native thread binding; the Codex harness additionally lets its mirror rebuild). This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery **once** and retry initialization before giving up:

1. stale-snapshot retry (unchanged — benign concurrent-revision case)
2. if still conflicted: run harness self-heal (`retireSessionMcpRuntime` + `resetRegisteredAgentHarnessSessions`) and retry init once
3. if it still cannot commit: throw with clear context (`…after harness self-heal retry`) instead of leaving the session able to silently return empty tool-results

The decision logic is isolated in a small pure helper (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts`) with unit tests.

## Testing
- `npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts` → 4/4 pass
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → no type errors in changed files (only pre-existing, unrelated errors in `src/plugins/providers.test.ts`)

## Scope
This addresses the conflict-wedge failure mode. It does not attempt to address a separate operational failure where the Codex app-server child is not running at all — a different cause that presents the same empty-tool-result surface.

target.title: [codex] Verify Telegram topic proof for cron delivery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cron jobs that deliver to a configured non-General Telegram forum topic could be marked delivered without Telegram proving the actual provider topic. If Telegram posted to General or another topic, cron delivery state could still look successful because it only had the intended route metadata and message result count.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram sends now surface provider-confirmed `chatId` / `messageThreadId` proof in `meta.telegram.messages[]`.

Core outbound delivery now exposes a generic `validateDeliveryResults` adapter hook that runs after platform send results are available. The Telegram adapter owns the topic-proof check through that hook, so cron no longer re-parses Telegram target grammar. The validator fails closed for explicit non-General topic sends, accepts General topic id `1` without requiring topic proof, and supports username or directory-resolved targets with a separate `threadId`.

## User Impact

Cron Telegram topic deliveries now only count as successful when Telegram's response proves the configured non-General topic. Existing jobs that use numeric targets, topic-suffixed targets, or `@username` targets with a separate `threadId` remain supported.

target.title: [codex] fix(feishu): preserve post markdown line breaks
target.body:
Fixes #97074

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu `post` messages render single markdown newlines as soft breaks, which can collapse normal agent output into cramped one-line paragraphs. Long Feishu replies are harder to read even when the source text has line breaks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Feishu send path already owns the final `tag: "md"` post payload. This change normalizes single line breaks at the Feishu-local post boundary after table conversion, while preserving existing blank lines and fenced code block line breaks.

After review, the newline expansion now participates in Feishu post text chunking instead of growing chunks after the 4000-character limit check. Normal outbound post sends and reply-dispatcher post replies expand newlines before chunking, then mark the chunks as already normalized before the final `sendMessageFeishu` call. Feishu document-comment targets keep the original chunker because those deliveries are not post+md messages.

A follow-up review noted that text edits still patched the normalized post payload directly. This branch now enforces the same 4000-character post text ceiling after newline normalization for direct post sends and post text edits. Over-limit edits fail before `client.im.message.patch`, while exactly-at-limit normalized edits still patch normally.

## User Impact

Feishu users should see normal paragraph-style breaks for ordinary agent output. Existing structured mentions stay native Feishu `at` elements, code fences keep their original internal line structure, newline-heavy post replies remain bounded by the Feishu text limit after expansion, and over-limit post edits now fail locally before sending an oversized patch request.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write --threads=1 extensions/feishu/src/send.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

Known proof gap:

- I do not have live Feishu client/API proof available from this local environment, so I cannot attach a redacted live rendering screenshot or API artifact. The added regressions cover newline expansion, near-limit chunk safety for outbound post sends and reply-dispatcher post replies, direct-send limit rejection, exactly-at-limit post text edits, and over-limit post edit rejection before patch.

Attempted but not completed:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu` was started for broader Feishu coverage, but it did not complete after several minutes with no failure output and was interrupted to avoid leaving a long local runner active.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted: yes. I used Codex to inspect the issue, check for duplicate PRs, implement the focused Feishu payload and chunking fix, address review feedback, and run the validation above.

target.title: fix(feishu): render single newlines as line breaks in post+md messages (#97074)
target.body:
Closes #97074.

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu's `post` payload with `tag: "md"` treats a single `\n` as a soft break, so standard markdown output with single-newline paragraph or list breaks renders mashed together on one line. Only blank-line-separated markdown creates a visible break. That makes multiline agent responses hard to read for users on the Feishu channel.

## Fix

`buildFeishuPostMessagePayload`, the builder for the `post` + `md` payload, now runs text through `upgradeFeishuPostNewlines()` before wrapping it as `{ tag: "md", text }`.

The helper:

- upgrades single `\n` to `\n\n` outside fenced code blocks
- leaves newlines inside fenced code blocks unchanged
- collapses 3+ newlines to 2 so gaps do not balloon
- trims leading and trailing blank lines introduced by the upgrade

The issue referenced `@larksuite/openclaw-lark` / `optimizeMarkdownStyle()`; in this repo the outbound `post` + `md` text is assembled in `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`, so the upgrade lives there.

## Evidence

Focused tests were added for:

- multi-paragraph and list input gaining paragraph breaks
- code-block newlines being preserved
- oversized gaps being collapsed
- existing single-line payload behavior remaining unchanged

Validation:

```text
extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts green (21 passing)
```

target.title: fix(daemon): refuse duplicate launchd gateway managers
target.body:
Closes #97178

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running the gateway under a system-domain LaunchDaemon could later run `openclaw gateway install` from a user session and silently add a duplicate gui-domain LaunchAgent for the same gateway label and port. That duplicate manager setup can restart-loop the gateway and disconnect clients.

## Why This Change Was Made

The macOS launchd installer now checks for a same-label system LaunchDaemon before it writes or bootstraps the user LaunchAgent. If `launchctl print system/<label>` succeeds or a matching `/Library/LaunchDaemons/<label>.plist` exists, install refuses with recovery guidance instead of creating a second KeepAlive manager. This intentionally stays narrow and does not add full system LaunchDaemon install/stop/uninstall lifecycle support.

AI-assisted: yes. I understand the change: it adds a pre-write launchd conflict guard and focused mocked launchd regressions for the reported duplicate-manager path.

## User Impact

Headless macOS operators who already manage the gateway as a system LaunchDaemon get a clear stop-and-fix error instead of a second user LaunchAgent that can fight the system daemon on the same port.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: `openclaw gateway install` refuses to write/bootstrap a gui-domain LaunchAgent when a same-label system LaunchDaemon is loaded or present on disk.

Real environment tested: local source checkout with mocked launchd states; the issue reporter supplied live headless macOS LaunchDaemon evidence on #97178. I did not mutate a real system LaunchDaemon on this host.

Exact steps:

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/inspect.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Evidence after fix: the new launchd tests cover both `launchctl print system/ai.openclaw.gateway` reporting a loaded daemon and `/Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` existing when the system job is not printed.

Observed result: focused launchd test passed; the broader daemon/status proof set passed in 2 Vitest shards.

What was not tested: live install against a disposable headless macOS host with a real system LaunchDaemon, to avoid creating or disturbing host-level launchd services from this automation run.


---

**Runtime proof — captured before/after (negative-control harness, macOS, Node 22):**

Exercised end-to-end through the real `installLaunchAgent` → `writeLaunchAgentPlist` → `assertNoSystemLaunchDaemonConflict` → real `execFile` path; only the external `launchctl` binary is mocked (a PATH shim), plist writes go to a scratch `HOME`. Same harness ran on unfixed `main` and on this branch.

_Before — unfixed `main` (negative control):_

```
Scenario A (no conflict, proceeds)  : PASS
Scenario B (conflict, refuses)      : FAIL
>>> UNFIXED: with a same-label system LaunchDaemon present, install did NOT
    refuse and WROTE the gui LaunchAgent plist anyway.  (the #97178 bug)
```

_After — this branch:_

```
Scenario A (no conflict, proceeds)  : PASS
Scenario B (conflict, refuses)      : PASS
error (verbatim): Existing system LaunchDaemon system/ai.openclaw.gateway detected at
  /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist. Refusing to install a gui-domain
  LaunchAgent for the same gateway label because duplicate launchd managers can
  restart-loop the gateway. ... sudo launchctl bootout system/ai.openclaw.gateway ...
plist written : false
>>> FIXED: the guard refused the duplicate manager with recovery guidance.
```

**What was not tested:** a live install against a disposable macOS host with a real system LaunchDaemon over a live port; and the on-disk `/Library/LaunchDaemons/<label>.plist` branch (needs a root-owned path via `sudo touch`/`rm`) — it shares the same throw site as the proven `launchctl print` branch.


---

**Branch-(b) proof — REAL root-owned `/Library/LaunchDaemons` plist (addresses the "mock-backed proof" review note):**

Re-ran on macOS with a genuine root-owned `/Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` (`sudo touch`), and with `launchctl print system/<label>` forced to report NOT-loaded (exit 113) so the **only** conflict signal is the real on-disk system plist — the `launchctl` shim plays no part in the decision. This exercises the real `/Library/LaunchDaemons` filesystem check (`LAUNCH_DAEMON_SYSTEM_DIR`) end-to-end.

_PR branch (`9f0f82df78`) — exit 0:_

```
launchctl print system/<label> : NOT-loaded (113)  -> branch-(a) inert
real /Library/LaunchDaemons plist present : yes     -> branch-(b) is the signal
install threw  : true
error (verbatim):
  | Existing system LaunchDaemon system/ai.openclaw.gateway detected at /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist.
  | Refusing to install a gui-domain LaunchAgent for the same gateway label because duplicate launchd managers can restart-loop the gateway.
  | Keep the system LaunchDaemon, or remove it first with `sudo launchctl bootout system/ai.openclaw.gateway` and `sudo rm /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist`, then rerun `openclaw gateway install`.
gui LaunchAgent written : false
>>> FIXED: install refused via the REAL root-owned system plist (branch-b).
```

_`main` (`29f5e9d35c`, no guard) — exit 1, negative control:_

```
launchctl print system/<label> : NOT-loaded (113)   real plist present : yes
install threw  : false
gui LaunchAgent written : true
>>> UNFIXED: install IGNORED the real system plist and wrote the gui LaunchAgent anyway — the #97178 bug.
```

target.title: fix(media): make wake-false direct fallback reason-aware
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#95910 tracks a focused follow-up to #86034: after successful media generation, `scheduleMediaGenerationTaskCompletion()` treated a `wakeTaskCompletion()` false return as an unconfirmed completion and closed the detached task as blocked, while the thrown wake path already had direct media recovery.

The unsafe fix would be to direct-send after every boolean `false`. That would recover some media-loss cases, but it also breaks the current no-send contract for `requester_abandoned` and unknown/generic false returns because the scheduler no longer knows why delivery failed.

This PR fixes that boundary by preserving the existing `wakeTaskCompletion(): Promise<boolean>` API and adding a media-internal detailed wake result so successful-generation closeout can still see the structured delivery reason before deciding whether direct fallback is allowed.

Fixes #95910.
Partial follow-up for #86034.
Supersedes the unsafe fallback boundary in #95945.

## Summary

- keeps the existing `wakeTaskCompletion(): Promise<boolean>` API for current media/tool callers
- adds a media-internal detailed wake result for scheduler closeout
- retries direct media delivery only for recoverable media-loss reasons:
  - `generated_media_missing`
  - `message_tool_delivery_missing`
  - `visible_reply_missing`
- keeps `requester_abandoned`, generic/no-reason false returns, and terminal delivery stops as no-send blocked outcomes
- adds scheduler-level regression coverage for the allowed reason, requester-abandoned, generic false, and thrown wake paths

## Behavior Matrix

| wake result | direct fallback? | terminal result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| delivered | no extra fallback | success |
| `generated_media_missing` / `message_tool_delivery_missing` / `visible_reply_missing` | yes, if direct channel origin is deliverable | clears blocked result on success |
| `requester_abandoned` | no | blocked |
| no reason / generic false | no | blocked |
| terminal delivery stop | no | handled as before |
| thrown wake after successful generation | existing direct recovery path remains | clears blocked result on success |

## Evidence

Local validation from this branch:

- Installed dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; lockfile was unchanged.
- Formatting check passed:
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.ts src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts`
- Relevant Vitest set passed: 5 files, 143 tests.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts src/agents/tools/image-generate-background.test.ts src/agents/tools/video-generate-background.test.ts src/agents/tools/music-generate-background.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- TypeScript core check passed:
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- Narrow lint passed:
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.ts src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts`
- Whitespace check passed:
  - `git diff --check`

Regression coverage added in `src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts`:

- detailed false with `generated_media_missing` and a deliverable origin calls direct fallback and clears `terminalResult`
- detailed false with `requester_abandoned` does not call `sendMessage` and remains blocked
- detailed false with no reason/generic error does not call `sendMessage` and remains blocked
- existing thrown wake direct recovery remains covered
- existing lifecycle-level tests still cover direct fallback through the old boolean wrapper and no-send behavior for requester abandonment/generic handoff failure

Mantis Telegram Desktop proof was attempted in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28294989921. The harness validated the selected refs, but the agentic Telegram proof job failed because the available Telegram setup could not reproduce the required generated-media completion wake-false condition. The uploaded `mantis-evidence.json` reported both baseline and candidate as `skipped`, with no video/artifacts produced.

That Mantis result is not behavioral proof that this PR works, and it is also not evidence that the candidate failed. It shows the current visible Telegram proof harness cannot trigger this internal delivery-result path. Current evidence remains the mocked scheduler and delivery-path coverage for the exact delivery-policy matrix changed by this PR.

Live gateway/channel proof remains open unless maintainers accept the scheduler boundary proof for this internal failure mode or provide/approve a live hook that can inject a recoverable `SubagentAnnounceDeliveryResult` such as `generated_media_missing` against a real channel.

target.title: Dashboard: control hub — per-agent nesting, shared/private tabs, presence
target.body:
# Dashboard: control hub — per-agent nesting, shared/private tabs, presence

> The multi-agent, multi-operator half of the vision: organize the dashboard by which agent built what, keep some tabs private, and see who else is in the workspace live.

Closes #101151, #101152, #101153. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff.

## What's in this PR
- **Per-agent nesting (#101151)** — group the tab strip by each tab's `createdBy` provenance, with a collapse/expand control to fold a whole agent's tabs away. Pure grouping over existing provenance.
- **Shared/private tabs (#101152)** — a tab may be `private`, visible only to its owner (enforced server-side, below).
- **Presence (#101153)** — a lightweight "who's viewing this tab" indicator over the existing broadcast path; the presence event carries `{ operator, tabSlug, at }` (id + tab only, never document state), ephemeral and never persisted.

## Security (private tabs)
Visibility is enforced **server-side**, not by hiding in the UI: every gateway response that serializes the workspace doc passes through `filterWorkspaceForOperator(doc, resolveOperatorIdentity(client))` (a `respondDoc` helper on `workspace.get`, every mutation response, `tab.create`, and `undo`), so a private tab the caller doesn't own is absent from the wire payload **and** the tab order. The store keeps the full doc; only the response is filtered. **Fail-closed:** an unidentified operator sees zero private tabs. (Operator identity is currently keyed on the paired **device id** — documented as the exact seam where a richer per-human identity threads in; a bootstrap-authed connection with no paired device can neither see nor own a private tab.)

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** With many agents and/or operators sharing one dashboard, there was no way to organize by agent, keep a tab private, or see concurrent activity. This adds per-agent grouping, server-enforced private tabs, and live presence.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` → 90 passed (visibility filter, fail-closed default, owner-only access, presence-payload shape — a private tab owned by A verified absent from B's serialized payload and tab order); `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/pages/plugin` → 119 passed (actor grouping/fold, presence store TTL + self-exclusion, visibility round-trip); `ui:i18n:check`, `ui:build`, full type-aware oxlint clean.

target.title: Verify signed marketplace feed refresh
target.body:
## Summary

- Wire signed marketplace feed profiles into hosted catalog refresh using the signed envelope verifier and configured threshold.
- Persist bounded signed-feed trust state with hosted snapshots, and re-verify signed snapshots with the current source profile before using them.
- Count signed-feed thresholds over unique normalized Ed25519 public-key material so duplicate key IDs or duplicate key material cannot weaken a multi-signature threshold.
- Keep signed profiles fail-closed on invalid live bodies or unsigned old snapshots, without changing install eligibility or the existing marketplace refresh/entries payload shape.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.test.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`

## Real behavior proof

Source harness from this branch generated an Ed25519 key, signed a hosted catalog feed envelope, loaded it through a signed feed profile, verified persisted snapshot trust state, then attempted offline fallback from an unsigned old snapshot under the same signed profile.

```json
{
  "acceptedSource": "hosted",
  "acceptedEntries": [
    "@openclaw/signed-proof"
  ],
  "acceptedTrust": {
```

target.title: Dashboard: ops widgets — agent status + approvals queue
target.body:
> The operational half of the builtin set: see what every agent is doing, and act on what's waiting for you — from a dashboard cell.

Closes #101145 and #101144. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review `agent-status.ts` + `approvals.ts` and their wiring as the delta.

## What's in this PR

**`builtin:agent-status` (#101145)** — a compact per-agent/session status list: active-run vs idle, current label, and freshness — the "what's everything doing right now?" glance. It binds to the same `sessions.list` data the `sessions` builtin already uses (no new backend), so it live-updates on the existing broadcast path.

**`builtin:approvals` (#101144)** — a pending-approvals queue with Approve/Deny actions, wired end-to-end through the **existing** widget-approval infrastructure from #101098 (`dashboard.widget.approve`): pending `custom:` widgets appear as cards, and a decision dispatches the same client path the Workspaces pending-card uses. The queue arrives via a new `ctx.approvals` source on the builtin context (mirroring the existing `ctx.embed` pattern), because it's in-memory workspace state rather than an RPC binding.

**Scope note (deliberate):** the gateway's exec/plugin approval RPCs (`exec.approval.*`, `plugin.approval.*`) exist and the app shell uses them, but they are operator-scoped and not in the dashboard's read-only binding allowlist (`DATA_READ_RPC_ALLOWLIST`). Widening that allowlist is a security decision we didn't want to smuggle into a widget PR — so this widget covers the dashboard's own approval queue today, and is shaped to take exec/plugin approvals as additional sources the moment maintainers bless that allowlist addition (called out in the module header). That keeps #72545 progressing without expanding any privilege surface.

## How it works
Both widgets follow the established builtin contract (`renderX(widget, value, ctx) => TemplateResult`), registered in `BUILTIN_WIDGET_RENDERERS` + `BUILTIN_KIND_PATTERN`. Agent-status is a pure mapper over the resolved `sessions.list` value. Approvals renders from `ctx.approvals` (built by the dashboard view from workspace state) and dispatches decisions through the existing, already-authorized `dashboard.widget.approve` method — this PR adds **no new gateway method and no new privilege**.

No new dependency — `pnpm-lock.yaml` unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** There's no cross-agent activity view in the dashboard (#101145 / the #39127–#54577 cluster), and approvals had no dashboard surface (#101144, advancing #72545) — operators had to open each session or wait for the pending-card to appear on the Workspaces tab. This adds two operational builtins: a live agent-status list and an approvals queue with working Approve/Deny.
**Evidence:** `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → 100 passed, including the new suites (status derivation filters + provenance, decision-vocabulary mapping + limit, populated/empty renders, and Approve/Deny wiring asserted against a mocked client dispatching `dashboard.widget.approve`); `pnpm ui:i18n:check` clean; `pnpm ui:build` and full type-aware oxlint clean; `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` green (schema kind additions).

target.title: Dashboard: stream + computed data-binding kinds
target.body:
> Live push feeds and derived values, not just files: bind a widget to a gateway event stream, or compute one from other bindings — safely, with no new network and no expression language.

Closes #101150. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the `schema.ts` / `index.ts` / `data-read.ts` deltas.

## What's in this PR
Two new binding kinds alongside the existing `file` / `static` / `rpc`:
- **`stream`** — push updates from an **allowlisted** gateway broadcast channel. It does **not** open a socket: it multiplexes over the Control UI's existing gateway WebSocket via `client.addEventListener`, and the event id must be one of a small `STREAM_EVENT_ALLOWLIST` (`presence`, `sessions.changed`, `plugin.dashboard.changed` — all read-only). Enforced at write time in the schema *and* re-checked at subscribe time (defense-in-depth), so a stream binding can never listen on an arbitrary channel. Unsubscribes on unmount.
- **`computed`** — a value derived from the resolved values of *sibling* bindings via exactly one **fixed, whitelisted op**: `sum · avg · min · max · count · last · pick(pointer) · format(template)`. It's a `switch` — **no expression language, no `eval`, no `Function`**. `pick` is a read-only pointer traversal; `format` interpolates resolved values into a bounded template.

**Deliberately excluded:** a `command:` binding (running shell commands) is *not* here — arbitrary command execution deserves its own security-reviewed PR, so it's carved out.

## How it works & why it's safe
`resolveBinding` gains branches on both sides (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/index.ts` client, `extensions/dashboard/src/data-read.ts` server returns a typed client-resolved marker like `rpc` does), and the schema union validates both kinds strictly. Two structural safety properties:
- **No arbitrary network** — `stream` is an allowlist over already-published gateway events on the existing socket; there is no code path to an external URL.
- **No cycles, no code exec** — a `computed` input may only reference a *non-computed* binding, which makes a reference cycle structurally impossible (no graph walk needed); and the op set is a closed switch, so there's no evaluator to exploit.

No new dependency.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Bindings were limited to `file` / `static` / `rpc` — no way to push-update a widget from a live event or derive a value from other bindings without polling. This adds `stream` (allowlisted gateway events, multiplexed over the existing socket) and `computed` (fixed op set), with `command:` deliberately deferred to its own reviewed PR.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` + `pnpm -C ui vitest run src/lib/dashboard` green — schema accept/reject for both kinds (unknown op, malformed inputs, non-allowlisted event, computed→computed rejection), each computed op's result, and stream subscribe→push→unsubscribe over a mocked event source; `pnpm ui:i18n:check`, `pnpm ui:build`, full type-aware oxlint clean. Counts confirmed by the submitting orchestrator's own gate run.

target.body:
Related: #96625
Related: #88838

## What Problem This Solves

Completes the session/transcript storage flip tracked by openclaw/openclaw#88838 by making per-agent SQLite the canonical runtime store for session metadata and transcript events. Legacy `sessions.json` and active transcript JSONL files are now doctor import inputs or archive artifacts, not runtime fallback state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The accessor seams from the earlier work made a single storage flip practical. Shipping a mixed file/SQLite runtime would let session metadata and transcript rows drift, so this PR moves import, runtime access, retention, SDK cleanup, and ratchets together behind the permanent accessor boundary.

## User Impact

Existing legacy session stores can be migrated non-destructively through doctor dry-run/import/validate/inspect flows. Runtime session creation, resume, transcript append, compaction, and maintenance use SQLite rows; retention still exports archived JSONL artifacts before deleting rows so support and archive workflows keep inspectable artifacts.

target.title: Dashboard: widget write-back — persist widget state via a setState bridge capability
target.body:
> Give sandboxed widgets memory: a jailed, approval-gated `setState` capability that turns custom widgets from views into stateful apps.

Closes #101137. **Stacked on #101098** (the sandboxed custom-widget host) — that PR lands first; this targets `main` with a cumulative diff, so review the new `state`-related files as the delta.

## What problem this solves
Custom widgets today are read-only: the postMessage bridge lets a widget *ask* the parent for data, but there's no way to *save* anything — so an agent-built notes pad, kanban, or game resets on every reload. This adds the one missing primitive: per-widget, jailed, size-capped state, without loosening the sandbox.

## What's in this PR
- New gateway RPCs `dashboard.widget.state.get` / `.set` (read/write scoped), persisting to a path-jailed, size-capped per-widget file under `<stateDir>/dashboard/state/<widgetId>.json` — atomic writes, kept *separate* from `workspace.json` (does not count against the 256 KB workspace cap).
- New bridge inbound messages `dashboard:setState` / `getState`, gated behind a new `state:persist` manifest capability (mirrors the existing `sendPrompt` gate).
- The trusted parent resolves the widget's own `widgetId` — a widget can never read or write another widget's state, and a widget-supplied id is ignored.
- Unit tests covering the store round-trip (persist → read-back), the 64 KB size-cap whole-reject, widget-id charset/traversal rejects, the capability gate, read/write scope, and state-vs-workspace separation — the `extensions/dashboard` suite (85 tests) and the UI dashboard suite (94 tests) are green.
- This PR is the capability + its plumbing; the first shippable consumer is the stateful notes/todo widget (#101146), which depends on it.

## How it works
The design mirrors the read path from #101098: **the widget never holds a credential and never talks to the gateway** — the trusted Control-UI parent brokers everything. On `dashboard:setState`, the parent calls `dashboard.widget.state.set` with the `widgetId` *it* already tracks for that iframe (`widget.id`); the widget's message carries only the opaque blob, and the `setWidgetState` bridge dependency takes *only* the blob — there is no code path by which a widget names another widget's state. State is capped at **64 KB** per widget (the serialized envelope, rejected whole *before* any write), stored under `<stateDir>/dashboard/state/<widgetId>.json` (`0o700` dir / `0o600` file), serialized through the store's process mutex and written atomically via `replaceFileAtomic`. The widget id is charset-guarded (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,48}$`) and the resolved path is re-checked for containment. The new `plugin.dashboard.widget-state.changed` broadcast carries `{ widgetId, version }` only — never the blob.

## Security
This widens the trust surface, so it carries the same adversarial-review discipline as #101098. Verified in code and tests:
- **(a) Own-state only** — the `widgetId` is always `widget.id`, bound by the trusted parent; the `setWidgetState` bridge dependency takes only the blob, and any id in the child's message is ignored.
- **(b) Size cap** — 64 KB enforced on the serialized envelope *before* any write; oversize is rejected whole (nothing written).
- **(c) Path jail** — the id is charset-guarded (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,48}$`) and the resolved `state/<widgetId>.json` path is re-checked for containment.
- **(d) Capability gate** — `state:persist` is required; an ungated widget is denied *without touching the gateway*, the same shape as `sendPrompt`.
- **(e) No new iframe reach** — the iframe still cannot reach the gateway; the parent holds the socket and calls the new RPCs on the widget's behalf.
- **(f) Sandbox unchanged** — opaque origin, CSP `connect-src 'none'`, and the window-identity accept filter are all untouched.

Note: this PR adds **no new dependency** — `pnpm-lock.yaml` is unchanged, so the dependency-graph guard should not trip.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Sandboxed custom widgets cannot persist their own state (the bridge is read-only), so any agent- or user-built interactive widget resets on reload. This adds a jailed, size-capped, capability-gated `setState`/`getState` path so a widget can save and restore its own state.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` → 85 passed (store persist/read-back round-trip, 64 KB whole-reject, widget-id charset/traversal rejects, capability gate, read/write scope, and proof that widget state is written under `state/<widgetId>.json` and never into `workspace.json`); `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → 94 passed (bridge routes `setState`/`getState` only when the `state:persist` capability is present, and ignores any widget-supplied id); `pnpm ui:build` and oxlint clean.

target.body:
> A notes pad on your dashboard that actually saves — and the pattern every stateful builtin after it will follow.

Closes #101146. **Stacked on #101329 (widget write-back)**, which is itself stacked on #101098 — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review `notes.ts` + the `buildBuiltinContext` host change as the delta beyond #101329.

## What's in this PR

- **`builtin:notes`** — an editable notes/todo pad. Content hydrates from persisted state on mount and saves on debounced input (~500 ms), so it survives reloads and stays consistent across two open browsers (the write-back broadcast triggers refetch).
- **A host-bound state accessor for builtins** — the piece that makes this safe and reusable. `BuiltinWidgetContext` gains an optional `state` accessor (`get`/`set`), and the dashboard view now builds the context **per widget** (`buildBuiltinContext`), closing over the host's own `widget.id` when it calls `dashboard.widget.state.get`/`.set`. A widget renderer never names a widget id — it can only ever touch its own state. This mirrors the trust model of the sandboxed path in #101329 (parent binds the id), applied to trusted builtins.
- **Graceful degradation** — with no connected client there's no `state` accessor, and the pad renders read-only with a hint instead of silently dropping writes.

## How it works
Builtins render in the trusted Control UI, so they use the write-back gateway RPCs directly rather than the sandbox's postMessage bridge — but the id-binding discipline is identical: the host supplies `widget.id`, never the renderer. The persist test drives the real `buildBuiltinContext` (not a hand-rolled mock) and asserts the RPC receives `{ widgetId: "notes-42", state: … }` — the id-binding itself is under test. State lives in the per-widget jailed store from #101329 (64 KB cap, atomic writes, separate from `workspace.json`).

No new dependency — `pnpm-lock.yaml` unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Operators want a scratchpad/todo on their dashboard, but before write-back (#101137/#101329) any editable widget reset on reload — and there was no pattern for a *builtin* to persist state safely. This adds a stateful notes builtin plus the host-bound per-widget state accessor that makes it (and future stateful builtins) possible.
**Evidence:** `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → 98 passed, including the four new notes cases (editable render, hydrate from mocked `state.get`, debounced persist through the real host-built context asserting the host-bound `widget.id`, and the read-only no-client fallback); `pnpm ui:i18n:check` clean; `pnpm ui:build` and full type-aware oxlint clean.

target.title: Dashboard: inter-widget pub/sub — a tab-scoped, parent-brokered message bus
target.body:
> Widgets on the same tab can finally talk to each other — a filter widget drives a chart, a selector narrows a table — without ever being able to reach a widget on another tab.

Closes #101147. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review `bus.ts` + the `bridge.ts` / host changes as the delta.

## What's in this PR
- Bridge messages `dashboard:publish` / `dashboard:subscribe` / `dashboard:unsubscribe` (inbound) delivering as `dashboard:message` (outbound), gated behind a new `bus:pubsub` manifest capability.
- A parent-brokered, DOM-free bus (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/bus.ts`): widgets never talk directly — the trusted parent fans a published payload out to the *other* same-tab subscribers on that channel.
- Caps: 8 KB payload, 60 publishes / 60 s (keyed by stable widget name so a remount can't reset the budget), 256-char channel names.

## Security model (this is the point of the design)
- **Tab isolation is structural, not a filter.** The subscription table is keyed `tabSlug → channel → subscriberId`, and a publish only ever iterates the *publisher's own tab bucket*. A widget on tab A cannot observe — or even enumerate — a subscriber on tab B; cross-tab delivery is unreachable code, not a rejected case.
- **Identity is broker-assigned.** The host mints an opaque `subscriberId` the widget never sees, and binds `tabSlug` from the widget's real tab (`tab.slug` in `renderGrid`) — both are closed over in the parent; a child message only ever carries an opaque `channel` + `payload`. A widget can't spoof another's identity, target a specific peer, or name a tab it wasn't assigned to. The publisher is excluded from its own broadcast.
- **No new reach.** The bus is in-memory and parent-brokered only — it never touches the gateway and never persists. The capability gate, size cap, and rate limit sit alongside the existing `sendPrompt` gates in `bridge.ts`; the `event.source` window-identity filter still guards the new inbound types; opaque origin unchanged.

All of the above is covered by tests (same-tab delivery, cross-tab non-delivery, publisher exclusion, capability denial both directions, size/rate caps, unmount teardown, unexpected-window rejection). No new dependency.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Dashboard widgets were fully isolated, so they couldn't compose — a filter widget had no way to drive a chart on the same tab. This adds a parent-brokered, tab-scoped pub/sub bus, capability-gated and rate/size-capped, with cross-tab isolation guaranteed by construction.
**Evidence:** `pnpm -C ui vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/components` green including the bus/bridge/host suites (tab-isolation, publisher-exclusion, capability gate, caps, unmount sweep); `pnpm ui:i18n:check`, `pnpm ui:build`, and full type-aware oxlint clean. Counts confirmed by the submitting orchestrator's own gate run (not agent-reported).

target.title: Dashboard: workspace time-travel + blame
target.body:
# Dashboard: workspace time-travel + blame

> Scrub your dashboard through its own history, diff any snapshot against now (grouped by who changed what), and click a widget to jump to the agent session that created it.

Closes #101822. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the history RPCs, `history.ts`, and the panel/blame UI as the delta.

## What's in this PR
- **Read-only history RPCs** — `dashboard.workspace.history.list` / `.get` (both `operator.read`) over the existing 20-entry undo ring. `list` returns `{ version, savedAt, bytes }` newest-first (metadata only, never bodies); `get(version)` returns one snapshot.
- **History panel** — a toolbar button opens a modal: the version list, a read-only preview render of any snapshot, a **diff vs current** grouped by actor (tab/widget added / removed / moved / retitled), and **restore** (wired to the existing single-step `dashboard.workspace.undo`, offered only on the newest snapshot).
- **Blame** — the cell menu shows "created by `agent:main` · vN"; for agent authors it links to the logbook (#99930) when that tab is advertised, so the dashboard becomes auditable and the logbook gains a spatial index.

## How it works
Everything is a **read-only** surface over state that already existed: the undo ring (snapshots), `workspaceVersion`, and `createdBy` provenance. The ring-read API parses ring files without mutating them; restore reuses the existing undo write (no new write RPC); the diff indexes widgets by id and tabs by slug across two docs. No new dependency, no new write privilege.

**Honest limitations (called out in-code):** restore is single-step (the ring is an undo ring, so only the most recent change is revertible); the logbook is a day-keyed snapshot journal with no URL-addressable session/day, so blame links to the logbook tab root rather than a specific entry; first-seen version resolves only once snapshot bodies are loaded (the panel), falling back to provenance-only.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** When agents co-edit an operator's dashboard, "what changed, who changed it, and why" had no answer — despite the substrate recording everything needed (undo ring, versions, provenance). This exposes it: history scrub, actor-grouped diff, restore, and widget→logbook blame.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` green (ring metadata/snapshot reads, RPC read-scope) + `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/pages/plugin` green (history loaders, `computeWorkspaceDiff` add/remove/move cases, `groupDiffByActor`, blame first-seen + graceful fallback); `ui:i18n:check`, `ui:build`, full oxlint clean. Counts verified by the submitting orchestrator's own gate: `extensions/dashboard` 83, UI dashboard + plugin-page + cell suites 138.

target.title: Dashboard: Living Answers + action-form — the chat↔dashboard loop
target.body:
# Dashboard: Living Answers + action-form — the chat↔dashboard loop

> Two halves of the flagship interaction: the agent answers show-don't-tell questions by composing a live widget, and widgets can act — a button or form that dispatches a parameterized prompt back to the agent.

Closes #101820 and #101821. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the `action-form`, `ephemeral`, and Living-Answers pieces as the delta.

## What's in this PR
- **`ephemeral` + pin (#101820)** — a widget may carry `ephemeral: { expiresAt }`; the store sweeps expired ephemeral widgets on read (one atomic write, only when something expired, version bumped), and a **Pin** action in the cell menu clears the marker to make it permanent. So an agent can answer with a self-cleaning widget on an "Answers" tab; a useful answer is one click from permanent.
- **`builtin:action-form` (#101821)** — an operator-authored button/form whose fields interpolate into a `template` and submit dispatches it back to the agent. "Deploy {env}", "Triage {id} as {priority}" become one-click playbooks.
- **Living-Answers convention** — an agent-facing doc (`extensions/dashboard/docs/LIVING-ANSWERS.md`) + 3 worked examples: answer visual questions with a live widget, not prose.

## Security (action-form)
- **No new dispatch privilege.** Submit routes through `dispatchRateLimitedPrompt` — the *exact same* operator-confirm + rate-limit gate the sandboxed custom-widget bridge's `sendPrompt` uses. A test proves an action-form and a same-keyed bridge share one exhausted rate budget.
- **No template injection.** Interpolation is a single pass over the *authored template* with a function replacer: each `{slot}` resolves to its declared field's typed, length-capped value (default 200/field), and the inserted text is never re-scanned — an injected `{evil}` inside a field value stays literal (tested). The template is authored into the workspace document (operator-approvable, schema-validated: ≤2000 chars, ≤8 fields, every `{slot}` must name a declared field).

## How it works
The `ephemeral` marker is a tiny schema addition swept in the store's existing read path; `action-form` is a trusted builtin registered like the others; the dispatch gate was extracted (`dispatchRateLimitedPrompt`) so the builtin and the sandbox bridge share one code path. No new dependency; no new gateway privilege.

Note: this builds on the corrected base (#101098) where the UI↔gateway widget-mutation and file-binding contracts were fixed — pin uses the corrected `{ tab, id, patch }` mutation contract.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** The dashboard could show data but not *act*, and agent answers to visual questions were prose that died in the transcript. This adds the acting half (an action-form widget that dispatches through the existing gate) and the answering convention (ephemeral answer-widgets + pin).
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` + `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/pages/plugin` green — schema validation (template/field caps, unknown-slot reject, ISO ephemeral), the store TTL sweep, the single-pass no-double-expansion interpolation, and the shared-rate-budget dispatch; `ui:i18n:check`, `ui:build`, full oxlint clean. Counts verified by the submitting orchestrator's own gate: `extensions/dashboard` 94, UI dashboard + plugin-page + cell suites 140.

target.title: fix(plugins): persist binding approval before trusting it in memory
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user picks **Allow always** on a plugin conversation-binding prompt, `addPersistentApproval` (`src/plugins/conversation-binding.ts`) published the grant into the in-memory approvals cache **before** the SQLite write that persists it. If that write throws — `SQLITE_BUSY` under concurrent writers, a full disk, a read-only or permission-denied state directory — the cache already held the grant while nothing was durably recorded, and there is no rollback.

The consequence is a silent, session-scoped over-approval: `hasPersistentApproval()` reads that cache and **auto-approves later binds for the same plugin/channel/account without prompting the user**, even though the triggering approval actually rejected (no binding was created, no "approved" event fired) and the grant is gone on the next restart. The user never durably granted a standing approval, yet the running gateway behaves as if they did until it restarts.

This is a default-path surface: plugin conversation-binding approvals are reached through the bundled Telegram, Slack, and Discord interaction handlers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime state must not end up more permissive than the durable store when a write fails. `addPersistentApproval` now **persists first** and only publishes the grant into the cache after the write succeeds, then recomputes the merged set from the current cache so a concurrently-approved grant is not dropped:

- On a write failure the cache is left untouched, so `hasPersistentApproval` stays `false` and the user is re-prompted — fail-safe, instead of a silent standing approval that was never saved.
- Publishing after the `await` recomputes from `getApprovals()` (not a stale pre-await snapshot), so two concurrent `Allow always` approvals both stay live in the cache. The `onConflict` upsert keeps the write idempotent.

The mutate-before-persist ordering pre-dated the JSON→SQLite move and the save-chain serialization change; neither added rollback. Scope is limited to `addPersistentApproval`; the save-chain serialization semantics and the separate before-tool-call plugin-permission approvals are unchanged.

## User Impact

A failed approvals write no longer leaves the gateway silently auto-approving plugin conversation binds that were never persisted. "Allow always" either persists and takes effect, or fails leaving no standing grant, so a later same-scope bind prompts again — the in-memory state matches disk in both cases. Successful and concurrent approvals are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Focused regression test (`src/plugins/conversation-binding.test.ts`): injects a write failure during an `Allow always` approval and asserts the approval rejects, nothing is persisted, and the next same-scope request stays `pending` (no auto-approval leak). Negative control: with the fix reverted the test fails with `bound != pending`.
- The existing concurrent "persists overlapping always-allow approvals" test was extended to assert both grants stay live in the in-memory cache (follow-up binds return `bound`). Negative control: a stale-snapshot variant fails this test.
- Local run against the real Vitest runner: `conversation-binding.test.ts` 19/19 pass with the fix; the two negative controls fail as expected with the fix reverted.
- **Real-behavior run** — a script drives the unmodified production functions (`requestPluginConversationBinding` / `resolvePluginConversationBindingApproval`) against a real `node:sqlite` state database, injecting a genuine `SQLITE_READONLY` write failure (`PRAGMA query_only=ON`, representative of a read-only / permission-denied / non-writable state database). No OpenClaw code is mocked — SQLite itself rejects the write:

  ```
  [setup] real state DB opened; PRAGMA query_only=ON -> writes raise SQLITE_READONLY

  == FAILURE PATH (approvals write fails) ==
  [fail] initial allow-always request -> pending  (expect: pending)
  [fail] allow-always resolve rejected -> true  (attempt to write a readonly database)
  [fail] persisted approval rows -> 0  (expect: 0)
  [fail] next same-scope bind -> pending  (expect: pending == NO in-memory auto-approval leak)

  == SUCCESS PATH (writes enabled) ==
  [ok]   allow-always resolve -> approved  (expect: approved)
  [ok]   persisted approval rows -> 1  (expect: 1)
  [ok]   next same-scope bind -> bound  (expect: bound == durable auto-approval)
  ```

  The failed write leaves no persisted row and, with the fix, no in-memory grant — the next same-scope bind stays `pending`. With writes enabled the same path persists the grant and auto-approves.
- `check:changed` / typecheck / lint delegated to hosted CI for this commit.
