target.title: fix: honor configured default agent across main paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the remaining hardcoded `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID = "main"` assumptions called out in #90573 for deployments whose configured default agent is not `main`.

PR #30654 fixed the main session-key write paths, but #90573 identified follow-on paths that still synthesized `agents/main/*`, `agent:main:*`, or phantom `main` audit scopes even when config declares a different default agent such as `nova`.

This PR uses the existing `agents.list[].default` / first-agent behavior. It intentionally does **not** add a new `agents.defaultAgentId` config key or `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` environment variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current behavior makes non-`main` default-agent deployments inconsistent: some surfaces honor the configured default agent, while others silently route storage, session keys, setup directories, or audit reporting through `main`. That creates broken paths and confusing phantom state for multi-agent installs.

## User Impact

Deployments whose configured default agent is not `main` can keep using their chosen default agent without residual `main` paths leaking into session initialization, auth/model storage scans, setup transcript directories, or exec-scope audit output.

## Changes

- Key new explicit `sessionId` sessions to the resolved store/default agent instead of literal `main`.
- Thread the resolved agent id into auto-reply session initialization.
- Resolve default auth/model storage scan paths from the configured default agent directory.
- Stop security audit exec-scope reporting from injecting a phantom `main` default when another agent is configured as default.
- Avoid inferring a delivery channel from one-segment agent main-session keys when the agent id happens to match a channel name.
- Let setup create the configured default agent's transcript directory instead of `agents/main/sessions` when config is available.

## Risk Mitigations

- **Compatibility:** no schema/env surface added; legacy `main` aliases are still recognized where they already were.
- **Auth-provider:** storage discovery still includes existing directories under state plus configured agent dirs; this only replaces the synthetic default path.
- **Session-state:** new explicit sessions use the same effective default agent that owns the selected store; existing persisted keys are not migrated here.

## Evidence

Current head: `8bbd81367e8807a741314b9a91cfb99d24b4586e`.
Current base: `6db0506474ceb10c64ea3b5f64e29772fb04280e`.

### Current-head runtime proof

Isolated config with `main` present and `ops` marked as `agents.list[].default` validates cleanly, and `agents list --json` reports `ops` as the default without promoting `main`:

```json
[
  {
    "id": "main",
    "isDefault": false,
    "agentDir": "<home>/.openclaw/agents/main/agent",
    "workspace": "<home>/.openclaw/workspace-main"
  },
  {
    "id": "ops",
    "isDefault": true,
    "agentDir": "<home>/.openclaw/agents/ops/agent",
    "workspace": "<home>/.openclaw/workspace"
  }
]
```

Direct runtime proof with configured agents `utility` and default `ops`, plus an existing on-disk `agents/main/agent` store, shows the new default surfaces consistently use `ops` while still discovering the old `main` store:

```json
{
  "defaultAgentId": "ops",
  "defaultAgentDir": "<state>/agents/ops/agent",
  "sessionKey": "agent:ops:main",
  "sessionStorePath": "<state>/agents/ops/sessions/sessions.json",
  "transcriptDir": "<state>/agents/ops/sessions",
  "authStoreAgentDirs": [
    "<state>/agents/ops/agent",
    "<state>/agents/main/agent",
    "<state>/agents/utility/agent"
  ],
  "modelsJsonPaths": [
    "<state>/agents/ops/agent/models.json",
    "<state>/agents/main/agent/models.json",
    "<state>/agents/utility/agent/models.json"
  ],
  "auditFinding": {
    "checkId": "agents.claude_cli.permission_mode_overridden_by_yolo",
    "severity": "warn",
    "detail": "claude-cli sets args=default, but OpenClaw exec is YOLO for: ops, utility, ops. Managed Claude live sessions use --permission-mode bypassPermissions."
  }
}
```

That covers the requested proof surfaces: session key/store path, setup transcript path, auth/model scan discovery, audit output, and explicit preservation/discovery of an existing `agents/main` store without treating `main` as the configured default.

### Local validation

- Focused default-agent tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/secrets/storage-scan.default-agent.test.ts src/agents/command/session.resolve-session-key.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-delivery.test.ts src/config/sessions/paths.default-agent.test.ts src/security/audit-exec-surface.test.ts` — passed 4 Vitest shards / 41 tests on current head.
- Core typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` — passed on current head.
- Formatting: `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` over the 14 touched files — passed on current head.
- Touched-file lint: `pnpm exec oxlint` over the 14 touched files — passed on current head.
- Whitespace: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passed on current head.
- Pre-PR preview: `~/.openclaw/workspace/scripts/openclaw-pre-pr.sh --repo /root/projects/openclaw-pr-51762 --plan-only` completed after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`.

GitHub checks are expected to re-run for this pushed head.

Closes #90573.
Supersedes stale #17477 without adding the previously proposed config/env fallback surface.

target.title: fix(installer): complete first-run onboarding
target.body:
## Summary

- send fresh installs into onboarding before doctor or gateway finalization probes
- use the just-installed OpenClaw binary for follow-up commands and explain `hash -r` when the shell still caches a removed path
- let onboarding persist gateway configuration and authentication before installing or starting the managed service
- preserve doctor, plugin update, gateway restart, and dashboard behavior for configured upgrades
- add installer regression coverage for fresh installs, upgrades, no-TTY behavior, stale PATH resolution, and gateway finalization

## What Problem This Solves

A fresh git install could report success without creating `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, gateway authentication, or a managed gateway service. Its suggested follow-up then failed first through a stale `/usr/bin/openclaw` shell lookup, and subsequently through missing gateway mode/auth/service state. The TUI also failed with `Missing gateway auth token` because setup had never completed.

This change makes first-run onboarding the installer finalization path. Doctor and gateway health behavior remain on the configured-upgrade path instead of being used as a substitute for initial setup.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts` (61 passed)
- `bash -n scripts/install.sh`
- `git diff --check`
- final structured autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings
- earlier exact-patch proof: formatting, ShellCheck, focused tests, onboarding/Crestodian Docker scenarios, gateway-auth tests, and the changed-files gate passed
- rebased patch ID matches the reviewed and tested pre-rebase patch

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Fresh `--install-method git --version main` installs could finish without first-run config, gateway auth, or a managed gateway service, then recommend commands that could not work in that state.

Real environment tested: Linux installer regression coverage plus onboarding/Crestodian Docker scenarios and gateway-auth scenarios on the same patch.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts`; `bash -n scripts/install.sh`; the existing Docker onboarding/Crestodian and gateway-auth scenario lanes were also run before the final rebase.

Evidence after fix: All 61 installer regression tests pass, including fresh-install onboarding, configured-upgrade doctor behavior, stale PATH handling, no-TTY guidance, gateway finalization ordering, and successful-upgrade dashboard behavior.

Observed result after fix: Fresh installs enter onboarding before doctor/gateway probes; setup owns gateway config and token creation before service installation; follow-up commands resolve the newly installed binary; configured upgrades continue through doctor and plugin update behavior.

What was not tested: The isolated black-box fresh install did not complete because dependency installation was still running after 23 minutes and was terminated. No successful full fresh-VPS install artifact is claimed.

target.title: Dashboard: apps layer — full-bleed tabs + widget gallery
target.body:
# Dashboard: apps layer — full-bleed tabs + widget gallery

> Two steps toward "every tab is a web app": a tab can be a single full-bleed widget, and widgets can be browsed and installed from a registry — through the same approval gate and sandbox as any custom widget.

Closes #101148 and #101149. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the full-bleed layout + gallery pieces as the delta.

## What's in this PR
- **Full-bleed tab (#101148)** — a tab may set `layout: "full"`, rendering a single widget filling the content area with no grid chrome; a menu toggle flips it. A custom widget can now *be* the tab — a real app surface.
- **Widget gallery + install-from-URL (#101149)** — browse a registry `index.json`, see the capabilities a widget requests, and install it. The **browser** fetches the index + bundle and sends only the fetched `{ name, manifest, files }` to a new `dashboard.widget.install` method (512 KB / 64-file caps).

## Security (gallery)
The gallery is the third-party-code surface, so it's deliberately conservative: **install is client-fetch only** — the gateway never receives or fetches a URL (a source-scan guard test asserts no `fetch`/`https` in the install path), so there is no server-side SSRF; the bundle is capped (512 KB, ≤64 files), path-jailed, extension-allowlisted, and run through the existing `validateWidgetManifest`; requested capabilities are surfaced *before* install. Installing never auto-approves and never bypasses the sandbox — an installed widget lands `pending`, passes the existing operator-approval gate (#101098), and runs in the same `allow-scripts`, opaque-origin, `connect-src 'none'` iframe as any custom widget.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** The dashboard couldn't express a full app-per-tab, and there was no supply side for widgets (everything hand-authored). This adds a full-bleed tab layout and an approval-gated, sandboxed install-from-registry path.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` → 92 passed (install caps, path jail, `pending` status, and a no-server-fetch source guard); `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/pages/plugin src/components` → 299 passed (gallery client-fetch + install, full-bleed render/toggle); `ui:i18n:check`, `ui:build`, and full type-aware oxlint clean. The 3 failures in the full suite are the pre-existing `terminal-panel` browser-fixture flake, unrelated to this change.

target.title: feat: add signed marketplace feed config
target.body:
## Summary

- extend marketplace feed verification config to support signed mode with local Ed25519 signing keys and an optional threshold
- validate signed feed trust anchors in the OpenClaw config schema, including key shape, strict raw base64url public-key parsing, private-key rejection, unique key IDs, unique normalized public keys, and threshold bounds
- document the new config fields in generated help and labels, and carry the verification shape into the official external catalog feed profile type
- fail closed for signed feed profiles until refresh envelope enforcement is wired, without fetching, reading snapshots, or returning bundled public entries for that selected profile

## Stack

- Stacked after #98299 (`feeds-trust-envelope-verifier`).
- This PR intentionally targets `main` as a draft because the dependency branch is on the fork; review should focus on the top commit `16cbe678ce` until #98299 lands.

## Scope boundaries

This is still a config-contract slice. It does not verify signed feed envelopes during marketplace refresh yet, does not persist snapshot trust state, does not add CLI/operator trust output, and does not change install eligibility. Signed profiles are accepted as local trust config but return zero marketplace entries until the later enforcement slice consumes signed envelopes.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxlint --deny-warnings src/config/zod-schema.ts src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/config/zod-schema.ts src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `codex review --base fork/feeds-trust-envelope-verifier` - clean after ClawSweeper/Codex hardening fixes

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
OpenClaw config now accepts signed marketplace feed verification profiles only when local Ed25519 public signing keys are provided and the optional threshold is valid. Invalid signed profiles fail schema parsing, including malformed raw base64url keys, duplicate key IDs, and duplicate normalized public keys. If a signed profile is selected before refresh envelope enforcement is wired, the hosted catalog loader fails closed by returning no entries and does not fetch the feed, read unsigned snapshots, or return bundled public catalog entries for that selected profile.

Real environment tested:
Windows source checkout at `C:\src\openclaw-feeds-trust-source-profiles`, stacked on #98299 head `8742cc6515`; source-level config schema tests, hosted catalog loader tests, targeted OpenClaw validation commands, and Codex review.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`
2. `pnpm exec oxlint --deny-warnings src/config/zod-schema.ts src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts`
3. `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/config/zod-schema.ts src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts`
4. `git diff --check`
5. `codex review --base fork/feeds-trust-envelope-verifier`

Evidence after fix:
The focused marketplace schema, generated-help quality, and hosted catalog loader tests passed with 23, 12, and 52 tests respectively. Targeted lint, targeted format, whitespace checks, and Codex review completed without findings.

Observed result after fix:
Signed marketplace feed config with valid local Ed25519 public keys and threshold parses successfully; missing keys, empty keys, invalid public keys, malformed raw base64url public keys, private PEM values, duplicate key IDs, duplicate normalized public keys, zero threshold, and threshold greater than key count are rejected. Selecting a signed feed profile before enforcement is wired returns a non-throwing fallback result with zero entries and does not call the fetch path.

What was not tested:
Live marketplace refresh of a signed envelope was not tested because this PR intentionally does not wire signed envelope enforcement into refresh or snapshot persistence yet.


### ClawSweeper proof refresh - signed config source harness

Current head: `16cbe678ce05e32d9dee9560520a72e13547f1a4`

Command:

```powershell
node --import tsx -
```

Output:

```text

PROOF:malformedRawKeyRejected=true
PROOF:malformedIssue=Expected Ed25519 public key as PEM or raw base64url
PROOF:duplicateTrustAnchorsRejected=true
```

This source harness used a generated Ed25519 public key and the real `OpenClawSchema` plus `loadConfiguredHostedOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEntries` path. target.title: fix(cron): keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat is disabled
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: When a cron job fires `sessionTarget: "main"` with `payload.kind: "systemEvent"` and default `wakeMode: "now"`, if the main-session heartbeat returns a non-retryable skip (e.g. `"disabled"`), the already-enqueued system event was removed and the job returned `status: "skipped"`. The event was silently lost — never delivered to the user.

**Solution**: Two-layer fix — (1) Timer layer: keep system event queued and request deferred heartbeat; (2) Heartbeat layer: bypass per-agent heartbeat config gates for cron-sourced wakes.

**What changed**:

- `src/cron/service/timer.ts`: In `executeMainSessionCronJob()`, the two branches that called `removeQueuedSystemEventHandle()` on heartbeat skip/error are replaced with a single branch that keeps the event queued, schedules a background heartbeat, and returns the original heartbeat status. Returning `"ok"` would cause one-shot jobs with `deleteAfterRun=true` to be immediately deleted, bypassing the bounded disabled-heartbeat retry mechanism.

- `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts`:
  - `runHeartbeatOnce()`: Wraps the `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent()` and `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs()` checks in `if (opts.source !== "cron")` — only non-cron sources are gated by per-agent config.
  - Scheduler `run()`: When a cron-targeted wake targets an agent not present in the heartbeat scheduler's agent list, calls `runOnce()` directly instead of returning `{status: "skipped", reason: "disabled"}`.

**What did NOT change**: The heartbeat-`"ran"` path (the common happy path) is untouched. No new dependencies, no config changes, no API surface changes.

Fixes #101537

---

## What Problem This Solves

System events like reminders, scheduled messages, and periodic notifications were silently lost when the main session heartbeat was disabled — a common state when the user hasn't interacted recently. The design flaw was coupling event delivery to immediate wake success.

Two layers contributed:
1. The timer layer was too eager to discard already-enqueued events when heartbeat failed
2. The heartbeat layer's per-agent config gates treated cron-sourced wakes the same as regular heartbeats, even though cron manages its own retry and scheduling policy

---

## Root Cause

**Layer 1 — Timer layer**: The system event was enqueued before the heartbeat attempt (line ~1990). When heartbeat failed, the cleanup code removed the event — discarding work already done.

**Layer 2 — Heartbeat layer**: `runHeartbeatOnce()` checked `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent()` and `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs()` unconditionally. Agents without explicit heartbeat config (e.g., `{id: "main"}` without `heartbeat: {every: ...}`) would always return `skipped/disabled` — even when the wake was triggered by cron. Additionally, the scheduler's `run()` returned `skipped/disabled` when the target agent was not in `state.agents` (agents without explicit heartbeat config are not tracked by the scheduler).

Together these two layers caused cron→main system event deliveries to fail silently on every attempt.

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat returns skipped/error; request background heartbeat instead of removing event. Bypass per-agent heartbeat config gates for cron-sourced wakes. Preserve skipped/error status so one-shot retry behavior and job visibility are maintained.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 / Node.js v24.1.0 / OpenClaw `fix/issue-101537-cron-main-systemevent-skip-disabled`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx vitest run` targeted test commands as shown below, each exercising real production functions at L2 level (real `runHeartbeatOnce`, real system event queue, real CronJob objects).

**After-fix evidence**:

L2+ evidence (real function calls, real objects, real system event queue):
```
$ npx vitest run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts -t "does not return disabled for cron"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 43 skipped (44)

$ npx vitest run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts -t "routes cron targeted wakes"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 25 skipped (26)

$ npx vitest run src/cron/service.main-job-passes-heartbeat-target-last.test.ts -t "does not skip with"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 3 skipped (4)

$ node --import tsx -e 'import { isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent } from "./src/infra/heartbeat-summary.js"; console.log(isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent({agents:{list:[{id:"worker", heartbeat:{every:"5m"}}, {id:"main"}]}}, "main"));'
false  ← gate rejects main; both fix layers now bypass this for cron

$ npx tsx evidence/pr-101668/run-evidence.mjs
=== L2 Evidence ===
1. System event enqueued, events in queue before: 1
2. applyJobResult called with status="skipped", error="disabled"
   shouldDelete: false (delete only on "ok")
   job.state.lastStatus: skipped, lastError: disabled
   Job in store: YES
3. Events in queue after: 1 (preserved)
```

Full regression suites:

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/25

## What Problem This Solves

Starts the hosted feed trust-verification implementation series by adding the signed envelope verifier primitives that later feed refresh and source-profile PRs can consume.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a small, isolated verifier for OpenClaw-hosted external plugin catalog envelopes. It verifies Ed25519 signatures over stable base64url payload bytes, accepts PEM or raw base64url public keys, validates the payload type, and only parses the feed after a trusted signature verifies.

This PR intentionally does not wire signed envelopes into marketplace refresh, config, snapshot persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility. Those stay in follow-up PRs from the RFC trust series.

The Ed25519 PEM/raw-key verification helpers are shared with device identity code so the new feed verifier does not fork a second signature implementation.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes yet. This is a draft implementation foundation for future signed hosted feed verification.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Signed hosted feed envelopes can be verified against an explicit trusted Ed25519 key, and payload bytes changed after signing are rejected before the feed is trusted.

Real environment tested:
Windows checkout `C:\src\openclaw-feeds-trust-envelope` at PR head `8742cc6515`; source harness using `node --import tsx -`; generated in-memory Ed25519 proof key; no network service or persisted cache involved.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Run a source harness that imports `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopePayload`, `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopeSigningInput`, and `verifyOfficialExternalPluginCatalogSignedEnvelope` from `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts`.
2. Generate an Ed25519 keypair, sign a minimal `clawhub-official-proof` feed envelope, verify it with the trusted public key, then change the payload sequence and verify the original signature no longer validates.

Evidence after fix:
```text
> node --import tsx -
PROOF:accepted=true
PROOF:signedBy=clawhub-root-proof
PROOF:feedId=clawhub-official-proof
PROOF:entryCount=1
PROOF:tamperedOk=false

```

Observed result after fix:
The verifier accepted the signed feed envelope with the trusted key and returned `signedBy=clawhub-root-proof`; the same signature rejected the tampered payload with `invalid-signature`.

What was not tested:
This proof uses a focused source harness with generated proof keys. It does not test live ClawHub hosted envelope publication, marketplace refresh wiring, config trust-root selection, snapshot trust-state persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility because those are intentionally deferred to later PRs in the trust series.

target.title: Fix container image upgrade migrations before gateway readiness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98565.

Replacing a Docker, Podman, or Kubernetes container image while preserving the mounted OpenClaw state volume could start `openclaw gateway run` directly and skip the startup repair/convergence work normally reached through `openclaw update` or `openclaw doctor --fix`. That let a gateway become healthy while state and plugin install metadata still reflected the previous image.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a shared-state startup migration checkpoint keyed to the current OpenClaw version.
- Gate foreground gateway startup on that checkpoint, while leaving probes like `gateway health` alone.
- Run startup state migrations and post-core plugin convergence under a shared SQLite lease before readiness.
- Heartbeat the lease during long startup work and verify lease ownership before recording the checkpoint.
- Keep checkpoint/lease acquisition behind the gateway startup guard, and avoid requiring the full shared-state schema to be canonical before doctor-style state repair can run.
- Fail closed for invalid config/state, startup migration warnings, lease loss, or plugin convergence errors; surface nonblocking plugin repair warnings without preventing startup.
- Document container image upgrade repair commands for Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes.

## User Impact

Routine container image upgrades with the same mounted state should converge automatically before the gateway reports healthy. If repair cannot complete safely, startup fails closed instead of serving with half-upgraded state; operators can run `openclaw doctor --fix` with the same image and mounted state volume, then restart. Nonblocking plugin repair warnings are logged but do not stop startup, matching the current `openclaw update` behavior more closely.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: Persist gateway restart audit events
target.body:
## Summary

- add durable `gateway_restart_audit` rows for restart scheduling/coalescing/rescheduling/deferral-bypass/emission events
- carry restart source/session/audit context through `/restart`, gateway restart tool, config writes, update runs, restart request API, and safe restart coordination
- persist safe-restart preflight details so incidents like `cron.isolated_agent_setup_timeout` can be attributed from state instead of inferred from timing

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart forensics currently loses the initiating reason/source for internal safe restart requests. In a real incident, the restart had to be reconstructed by correlating a cron isolated-agent setup timeout with the default 300s safe-restart deferral and a later `SIGUSR1` restart log. That leaves avoidable ambiguity between internal restart requests and external/manual signals.

This change writes durable audit records when restart requests are scheduled, coalesced, rescheduled, bypass deferral, or emit the restart signal. The audit captures reason/source/session metadata plus safe-restart preflight context so future incidents can be attributed directly from state/log evidence.

target.title: fix(workspace): prevent false Missing labels on existing files and fix panel layout overlap
target.body: Fixes two bugs in the session workspace side panel where files referenced by tool calls outside the workspace root were incorrectly shown as "Missing",and the panel layout would visually overlap when many files were present. Note: the root-path leading-dot issue reported in the same issue (#96660) was already resolved separately. The remaining two bugs were reproduced with screenshots attached below. Fixes #96660 ## What Problem This Solves - False "Missing" badge on existing files Fixes an issue where the "Expand Session Workspace" side panel would show a red "Missing" badge on files that actually exist on disk (e.g. /tmp/foo.txt). Any tool-call path outside the workspace root was unconditionally flagged as missing because resolveTouchedFilePath returns undefined for external paths, and statWorkspacePath can fail to reach them through the workspace sandbox. - Side panel layout overlap Fixes a layout bug where the section headers, search input, and file rows in the side panel would visually overlap when the file list grew large, making the panel unreadable. - Regression in sessions.files.get error type The directStat fallback (item 1) introduced a regression: when sessions.files.get requested content for a file outside the workspace, directStat returned { missing: false } without content, causing the handler to emit session_file_too_large instead of the correct session_file_not_found. Fixed by skipping directStat when includeContent is requested, since we can never safely serve file content for paths outside the workspace sandbox. ## Why This Change Was Made A directStat helper was added that uses fs.existsSync + fs.statSync as a best-effort fallback before marking a file as missing. This runs in two places: (1) when the resolved path is outside the workspace root, and (2) when the workspace sandbox fails to stat the path. The fallback is only used for the list view (sessions.files.list), where content is not needed — stat metadata alone is sufficient. When content is requested (sessions.files.get), paths that can't be reached through the sandbox are treated as not found, preserving the original error semantics. The CSS fix adds flex-shrink: 0 to .chat-workspace-rail__section and its title so flex containers cannot compress sections below their content height, which was causing the overlapping layers. ## User Impact Users opening the session workspace side panel will no longer see false "Missing" badges on files that exist on disk but are outside the workspace root. The panel layout remains stable and readable even with many files, artifacts, and browser entries. ## Evidence Verified locally by creating files at `/tmp/a.txt` ... via tool calls, then confirming the workspace panel shows them without the red "Missing" badge in both Changed and Read sections. The panel layout no longer overlaps after refreshing with many files present. the screenshots attached below.

target.title: fix(exec-approval): distinguish non-persistable command from ask=always policy in approval prompt
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When \`allowAlwaysPersistence.kind === "one-shot"\` (for example, a command that uses shell redirection), \`allow-always\` is correctly excluded from the allowed decisions. The approval prompt still showed the same explanation used for an \`ask=always\` policy:

> "The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable."

That is misleading because the command can be approved; it just cannot be saved as a reusable approval pattern.

Closes #97069

## What Changed

1. **`exec-approval-reply.ts`** — added optional `nonPersistableCommand` field to `ExecApprovalPendingReplyParams`. When true, `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload` emits a distinct message explaining the command cannot be saved as a reusable pattern.

2. **`bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts`** — same branch added to `buildApprovalPendingMessage` (the foreground/CLI approval message path).

3. **`bash-tools.exec-types.ts`** — added `nonPersistableCommand?: boolean` to the `approval-pending` variant of `ExecToolDetails`, so the flag survives the gateway→tool-result→embedded-handler hop.

4. **`bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts`** — `buildExecApprovalPendingToolResult` accepts and passes `nonPersistableCommand` through to both the message builder and the details output.

5. **`bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts`** — derives and passes `nonPersistableCommand: effectiveAllowAlwaysPersistence.kind === "one-shot" && hostAsk !== "always"` to the tool-result builder.

6. **`bash-tools.exec-host-node.ts`** — same derivation using `allowAlwaysPersistence` and `approvalDecisionAsk`.

7. **`embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts`** — reads `nonPersistableCommand` from the pending details and forwards it to `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload`.

8. **`exec-approval-forwarding.ts` (Telegram)** — derives `nonPersistableCommand` from `allowedDecisions` and `request.request.ask` and passes it through.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Unit tests — 188 passing across 5 test files:**

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/exec-approval-reply.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-shared.test.ts \
```

| Gateway foreground (`buildApprovalPendingMessage`) | always policy copy | ✅ correct copy |
| Gateway tool result details (`ExecToolDetails`) | no flag | ✅ flag stored |
| Embedded handler → reply payload | no flag | ✅ flag forwarded |

| Node foreground | always policy copy | ✅ correct copy |

target.title: fix(approval): distinguish policy vs non-persistable reason when Allow Always unavailable
target.body:
Fixes #97069.

## What Problem This Solves

When a command includes shell redirection (e.g. `openclaw --version 2>&1`), Allow Always is correctly hidden because one-shot commands can't be safely persisted. But all nine approval prompt renderers (reply, forwarder, agent-facing, Control UI, reaction, embedded handler, Telegram handler, Telegram forwarding, and gateway API) incorrectly blame the effective approval policy—even when the effective policy is `ask=on-miss`. Users waste time misdiagnosing their approval policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is that `resolveExecApprovalAllowedDecisions()` returns the same `["allow-once", "deny"]` for both `ask=always` (policy) and one-shot persistence (non-persistable command). Downstream renderers can't tell the difference.

Rather than introducing a new typed protocol field (`allowAlwaysUnavailableReason`) — which #97081 attempted across 65 files — we thread the existing `ask` field (already present in `ExecApprovalRequestPayload`, `ExecApprovalPendingReplyParams`, `PendingApprovalView`, Control UI request state, and the gateway/node host pipeline) through the approval-pending data pipeline so all renderers can branch on it.

The fix is at the renderer layer, not the policy decision layer. Approval policy logic is unchanged.

## Root Cause

`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts:1824` — `resolveExecApprovalAllowedDecisions()` collapses both reasons (ask=always policy and one-shot persistence) into a single return value. Nine renderers check `!allowedDecisions.includes("allow-always")` and unconditionally emit the policy message.

Introduced by: gumadeiras `ba735d015809` (generic unavailable copy)
Made visible by: jesse-merhi `c9707ab635b9` (one-shot persistence for shell-redirected commands)
Confidence: clear

## User Impact

Users with `ask=on-miss` (or any non-always policy) who run commands with shell redirection will now see:

> Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).

Instead of the misleading:

> The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable.

Users with `ask=always` see the same policy message as before.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Approval prompt text blames policy when missing Allow Always is actually caused by one-shot/non-persistable command safety.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v22.11.0, branch `fix/exec-approval-prompt-text-97069`, base commit `origin/main`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

**Reply renderer** (the function that builds gateway-to-channel approval prompts):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload } from './src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts';

console.log('=== ask=always ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload({
  approvalId: 't1', approvalSlug: 's1',
  ask: 'always', allowedDecisions: ['allow-once', 'deny'],
  command: 'openclaw --version 2>&1', host: 'gateway',
}).text);

console.log('=== ask=on-miss ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload({
  approvalId: 't2', approvalSlug: 's2',
  ask: 'on-miss', allowedDecisions: ['allow-once', 'deny'],
  command: 'openclaw --version 2>&1', host: 'gateway',
}).text);
"
```

**Forwarder renderer** (real `ExecApprovalRequest` objects through the channel-forwarding path):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { buildExecApprovalRequestMessage } from './src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.ts';

var now = Date.now();
var req = {
  id: 'exec-req-1', createdAtMs: now, expiresAtMs: now + 300000,
  request: { command: 'openclaw --version 2>&1', cwd: '/home/user/project',
    host: 'gateway', agentId: 'main', security: 'allowlist' },
};

console.log('=== ask=always + allow-always excluded ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalRequestMessage(
  { ...req, request: { ...req.request, ask: 'always' } }
));

console.log('=== ask=on-miss + allow-always excluded ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalRequestMessage(
  { ...req, request: { ...req.request, ask: 'on-miss', unavailableDecisions: ['allow-always'] } }
));
"
```

**Evidence after fix** — real production renderer output:

**Reply renderer**:

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "..."

=== ask=always ===
The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable.

=== ask=on-miss (one-shot) ===
Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).
```

**Forwarder** (real `ExecApprovalRequest` objects — same shape as the gateway production path):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "..."

=== ask=always + allow-always excluded ===
🔒 Exec approval required
...
Allow Always is unavailable because the effective policy requires approval every time.

=== ask=on-miss + allow-always excluded ===
🔒 Exec approval required
...
Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).
```

**Telegram approval paths** (same renderer called by `buildTelegramExecApprovalPendingPayload` and `approval-handler.runtime.ts`):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "import ... from './src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts'; ..."

=== Telegram: ask=on-miss + allow-always excluded ===
Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).

=== Telegram: ask=always + allow-always excluded ===
The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable.
```

| `ask` input | Message shown |
|---|---|
| `"always"` | "The effective approval policy requires approval every time…" (unchanged) |
| `"on-miss"` (one-shot) | "Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted…" (fixed) |
| `"off"` (full-auto with shell redirect) | "Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted…" (fixed) |
| absent / null (plugin, legacy) | "The effective approval policy requires approval every time…" (safe default) |

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/infra/exec-approval-reply.test.ts \
    src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts \
    src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts \
    extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.test.ts \
    ui/src/components/exec-approval.test.ts
# all passed (with fix in commit 700f47c for approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts — see below)
```

**Observed result after fix**: All nine approval prompt renderers now show the appropriate message. Policy → policy text, one-shot → non-persistable text, absent ask → policy (safe default). Production pipeline (gateway + node hosts → ExecToolDetails → embedded handler) threads `ask` through. The node path uses `approvalDecisionAsk` (`maxAsk(hostAsk, nodeAsk)`) — keeping the reasoning consistent with `allowedDecisions` computation. Telegram native and forwarding paths pass `ask` through `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload`. Gateway API error path uses the same `isPolicyAlways` heuristic.

Additional CI guard checks pass locally: `pnpm build:plugin-sdk:strict-smoke` (dts emit), `pnpm ui:i18n:check` (all locales clean).

**End-to-end Telegram pipeline proof**: The terminal renderer output is byte-identical to what the Telegram Bot API `sendMessage` endpoint receives. The pipeline has three layers with zero text transformations:

1. `buildPendingPayload()` (`approval-handler.runtime.ts:75`) → `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload({ask, ...})` → returns `{ text, buttons }`
2. `deliverPending()` (`approval-handler.runtime.ts:162`) → `sendMessage(chatId, pendingPayload.text, {...})` — `pendingPayload.text` IS the Layer 1 result, passed verbatim
3. `sendMessageTelegram()` (`send.ts`) → calls Telegram Bot API `sendMessage` — text parameter passed without modification

No escaping, no MarkdownV2 transformation, no string manipulation occurs between layers. Therefore the terminal output above is the exact text Telegram displays.

**Test fix (commit 700f47c)**: The `approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts` test "shows non-persistable reason in reaction prompts" initially used `allowedDecisions: ["allow-once", "deny"]` in the request payload. However, `buildPendingApprovalView()` → `resolveExecApprovalRequestAllowedDecisions()` computes decisions from `ask` + `unavailableDecisions` — it does **not** read `allowedDecisions` from the request. The field was silently ignored, `allow-always` was never excluded, and the test couldn't trigger the non-persistable message path. Fixed by changing to `unavailableDecisions: ["allow-always"]`, which correctly feeds into `resolveExecApprovalRequestAllowedDecisions()`. The other two new tests (reply + forwarder) call `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload()` directly with `allowedDecisions` in the payload params, not the request — that path uses the field correctly via `resolveAllowedDecisions()`.

## Regression Test Plan

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/infra/exec-approval-reply.test.ts \
    src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts \
    src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts \
    extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.test.ts \
    ui/src/components/exec-approval.test.ts
# all pass
```

New test cases added:
- `exec-approval-reply.test.ts`: "shows non-persistable reason when allow-always is excluded for non-policy reasons"
- `exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts`: "shows non-persistable reason when allow-always excluded for non-policy reasons"
- `approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts`: "shows non-persistable reason in reaction prompts when allow-always excluded for one-shot"

## Changes

- `src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts`: +5/−1 — branch on `params.ask` in reply renderer
- `src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.ts`: +5/−1 — branch on `request.request.ask` in forwarder
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts`: +6/−1 — accept `ask` in agent-facing pending message
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-types.ts`: +1 — add `ask` to `ExecToolDetails` approval-pending
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts`: +3 — thread `ask` through `buildExecApprovalPendingToolResult`
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts`: +1 — pass `hostAsk` to pending tool result
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.ts`: +2 — pass `approvalDecisionAsk` to pending result and request registration (not raw `hostAsk` — matches the `maxAsk(hostAsk, nodeAsk)` value used to compute `allowedDecisions`)
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts`: +3 — read and forward `ask` from details
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.ts`: +7/−1 — branch on `ask` in reaction manual instruction, with `approvalKind === "exec"` discriminator guard for `PendingApprovalView` union type
- `extensions/telegram/src/exec-approval-forwarding.ts`: +1 — pass `params.request.request.ask` to reply payload
- `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts`: +1 — pass `params.view.ask` (exec only) to reply payload
- `src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approval.ts`: +10/−7 — distinguish policy vs non-persistable in validateDecision error message
- `ui/src/components/exec-approval.ts`: +11/−3 — use `allowAlwaysNonPersistable` i18n key for non-policy
- `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`: +2 — new `allowAlwaysNonPersistable` key
- `ui/src/i18n/`: sync-generated fallback keys for all other locales
- 3 test files: +54 new tests covering one-shot render path

---

**Update (2026-06-30)**: Rebased onto latest main and fixed `ui/src/i18n/.i18n/raw-copy-baseline.json` baseline drift (upstream PR #92654 added "Cancel reply" strings to `chat.ts` but forgot to sync the baseline — not a bug in this PR). All CI checks now pass. No source changes were needed beyond the baseline sync.

target.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup
target.body:
Fixes #75658

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run` did not preview stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files, and the apply summary did not report when those physical archive files were removed. Operators could see only unreferenced-artifact counts even when deleted/reset session archives were the files consuming disk.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cleanup command already had an archive retention helper, but dry-run did not call it and store maintenance discarded its removal count. This change reuses the existing archive-retention rules for both preview and apply reporting instead of adding a second cleanup policy.

Reviewer follow-up: dry-run cleanup now mirrors apply ordering. Deleted/reset archive cleanup is previewed before disk-budget enforcement, and the disk-budget sweep excludes paths already attributed to archive cleanup. This keeps dry-run `archiveCleanup` and `diskBudget` attribution aligned with apply output.

## User Impact

Users running `sessions cleanup` now see deleted/reset archive cleanup in dry-run output and in apply output. Forced cleanup also scans the store directory for stale deleted archives even when no session rows were removed, while `resetArchiveRetention: false` still preserves reset archives.

## Evidence

Focused validation:

- `CI=true pnpm run lint:tmp:session-accessor-boundary`

## What Problem This Solves

The Android app had a read-only Skills settings surface while the Control UI already supports a fuller skills-management workflow. Android users could inspect gateway skill status, but they could not search installed skills, turn skills on or off, or install skills from ClawHub from the app.

This PR brings the requested Android skills-management path closer to the existing Control UI behavior while keeping Gateway policy as the source of truth.

## Summary

- Extend Android Skills settings from read-only status into a management surface with installed-skill search, Web-aligned status filters, and per-skill enable/disable via `skills.update`.
- Add ClawHub registry search and install from Android via `skills.search` / `skills.install`.
- Add an Android pre-install ClawHub audit review dialog before downloading a skill. The dialog resolves and displays:
  - skill name / slug
  - resolved install version
  - author / publisher
  - ClawHub audited safety result
  - security audit URL when provided
- Extend `skills.securityVerdicts` with a bounded explicit `items[]` request shape so clients can request pre-install review verdicts for known ClawHub slug/version pairs.
- Keep the security boundary server-side: Android cannot pass an arbitrary registry URL for verdict lookup; explicit verdict lookups resolve through the configured default ClawHub registry.
- Preserve Gateway trust enforcement: Android may acknowledge non-blocked review-required installs only from the review dialog; blocked/malicious releases remain blocked by Gateway policy.
- Parse `blockedByAgentFilter` for accurate Android skills status and keep the Android README/i18n inventory current.

- `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts`

target.title: fix(heartbeat): harden commitment check-in delivery
target.body:
## Summary

Commitment-only heartbeat runs use OpenClaw's built-in inferred-commitment prompt, which can bypass `HEARTBEAT.md`. This hardens that path so inferred-commitment check-ins stay usable and conversation-aware.

## Problem

We observed Telegram receiving an inferred-commitment heartbeat message that began with visible reasoning:

```text
think
The user's message is a heartbeat poll.
...
If your wife has posted in Travel Agent, I can grab her Telegram ID and update the topic access.
```

The existing commitment prompt already tells the model not to mention commitment machinery, but it does not tell the model to suppress visible analysis/reasoning preambles. Deployments that add that guard in `HEARTBEAT.md` are still exposed because commitment-only runs can use `buildCommitmentHeartbeatPrompt` directly.

There is also a follow-on usability gap: a visible heartbeat check-in can be delivered to Telegram without being mirrored into the source session transcript. When the user replies to that check-in in Telegram, the agent may not see the proactive message it is replying to.

## Fix

- Add a no-visible-reasoning/no-preamble instruction to `buildCommitmentHeartbeatPrompt`.
- Keep the instruction narrowly scoped to final visible heartbeat output: either concise check-in text or exactly `HEARTBEAT_OK`.
- Mirror visible heartbeat deliveries into the base session transcript so user replies have the proactive check-in in conversation history.
- Pass the owning session-store path through delivery mirror metadata so mirrors append to the correct store, including custom/test session stores.
- Add regression coverage in the existing commitment heartbeat tests for both the prompt guard and transcript mirror behavior.
- Add an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a disposable local heartbeat with a fake Telegram transport and redacted identifiers. The run used the real `runHeartbeatOnce` delivery path, a pending inferred commitment scoped to `agent:main:telegram:user-redacted`, and a mocked model reply that verified the prompt contained the no-reasoning/no-`think` guard before returning a visible check-in.

```json
{
  "result": {
    "status": "ran",
    "durationMs": 5198
  },
  "telegramSends": [
    {
      "to": "redacted-chat-id",
      "text": "If the Travel Agent post is available, I can update the topic access.",
      "accountId": "primary"
    }
  ],
  "commitment": {
    "id": "cm_pr_proof",
    "status": "sent",
    "attempts": 1,
    "sentAtMs": 1778269543261
  },
  "transcript": {
    "fileBasename": "proof-session.jsonl",
    "hasDeliveryMirror": true,
    "hasVisibleCheckIn": true,
    "hasVisibleThinkLeak": false,
    "tail": [
      {
        "type": "session"
      },
      {
        "type": "message",
        "idempotencyKey": "heartbeat:commitments:agent:main:telegram:user-redacted:cm_pr_proof",
        "role": "assistant",
        "provider": "openclaw",
        "model": "delivery-mirror",
        "text": "If the Travel Agent post is available, I can update the topic access."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

This demonstrates that the visible check-in is delivered to the Telegram-equivalent transport, does not include a visible `think` leak, marks the commitment sent, and appends the same check-in as a `delivery-mirror` assistant message to the source session transcript.

## Test Plan

- `pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.commitments.test.ts`
- `pnpm check:changed`

## Notes

I checked open PRs/issues first. There are several related thinking/reasoning leak fixes, and PR #75469 touches inferred-commitment heartbeat scheduling. PR #79502 mirrors Telegram outbound replies in another delivery path, but I did not find an open PR covering commitment heartbeat prompt leakage plus heartbeat delivery mirroring.

target.body:
## Summary

Keeps OpenClaw's recommended NVIDIA Endpoint models aligned with NVIDIA's authoritative seven-row featured-model catalog while preserving `minimaxai/minimax-m2.7` metadata for exact-reference compatibility. New onboarding and selectable catalog surfaces expose only the seven current featured models.

### What Problem This Solves

NVIDIA Endpoint users could see outdated recommended models and metadata after NVIDIA updated its featured catalog. Removing every old row would also discard metadata needed by existing M2.7 configurations.

## Changes

- Refresh the bundled selectable catalog with Nemotron 3 Ultra, Nemotron 3 Super, GLM 5.2, Kimi K2.6, MiniMax M3, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and Qwen3.5 397B A17B using values from NVIDIA's featured-model JSON.
- Retain `minimaxai/minimax-m2.7` as a deprecated exact-reference row in the full NVIDIA provider catalog.
- Route NVIDIA onboarding, static selection, live selection, and augmented picker catalogs through selectable-only builders so M2.7 does not appear in new model choices.
- Keep retired same-line IDs out of OpenClaw's catalog; NVIDIA's hosted provider handles those aliases server-side.
- Match feed-provided names, context windows, and max-output values: Ultra is `1,048,576 / 8,192`, Super is `1,000,000 / 8,192`, and DeepSeek/Qwen are `262,144 / 16,384`.
- Update NVIDIA provider documentation and focused catalog/onboarding tests.

### Why This Change Was Made

NVIDIA's public `featured-models.json` is the source of truth for current recommendations. The NVIDIA plugin now separates the full metadata catalog from selectable surfaces: current models remain easy to choose, while existing M2.7 users retain exact-reference metadata across the M2.7 → M3 major-version boundary.

## Validation

### Evidence

Closes #101348

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw supports Docker-backed agent sandboxing and separately supports running the Gateway under Podman, but Podman-first users do not have a supported local container backend for sandboxed agent tools. They currently need Docker, an unsupported Docker-compatible shim/socket path, or a non-container sandbox backend.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a bundled `podman` sandbox plugin that registers a first-class Podman backend through the existing sandbox backend SDK, while reusing the Docker-compatible sandbox container settings for image, mounts, env, network, capabilities, tmpfs, setup commands, and resource limits. The implementation keeps browser sandboxes and Docker GPU support fail-closed for Podman, preserves Docker-specific user fallback behavior, and maps Podman no-network sandboxes correctly into Codex external sandbox policy.

## User Impact

Users can set `agents.defaults.sandbox.backend: "podman"` to run agent sandbox commands in rootless Podman containers. Writable workspace mounts work with default rootless Podman through `keep-id`, policy/doctor can observe Podman container posture, and `openclaw sandbox` lifecycle operations can describe and remove Podman runtimes.

target.title: fix(memory-core): guard supplement lookup in resolveMemoryReadFailureResult with try-catch (fixes #101809)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `memory_get corpus=all` primary read fails, the tool calls `resolveMemoryReadFailureResult` which attempts supplement lookup via `getSupplementMemoryReadResult()`. If the supplement lookup throws (e.g., config loading or database issue), the error propagates as an unhandled rejection because:

1. `resolveMemoryReadFailureResult` is **already inside the outer `catch` block** of `executeMemoryReadResult`
2. The supplement call inside it **has no try-catch guard**
3. The error escapes as an unhandled rejection instead of returning the structured `{disabled: true}` error result

Fixes #101809.

## Changes

### `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts`

Wrap the supplement lookup call in `resolveMemoryReadFailureResult` with try-catch. When supplement lookup fails, fall through to return the original primary memory-read structured error (`{path, text: "", disabled: true, error: "..."}`) instead of crashing.

### `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts`

Add proof test `"returns structured error when supplement lookup throws in memory_get corpus=all fallback"`:
1. Primary memory read throws
2. Registered corpus supplement `get()` throws
3. Asserts the result is the **original primary disabled result** (`error` contains "primary read failed", does NOT contain "supplement lookup failed")

## Evidence

**Unit tests (23/23 passed):**
```

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  23 passed (23)

```

**Real behavior proof — before fix (test fails, uncaught exception):**

target.title: fix(runtime): drop intermediate monologue text blocks from visible delivery
target.body:
## Summary

Fix Discord main-session replies leaking model thinking content for providers
like MiniMax-M3 via the openai-completions API.

The fix is in the shared assistant-text extraction layer
(`src/shared/chat-message-content.ts`) rather than the Discord plugin, because
the same root cause affects every channel that reads `extractAssistantVisibleText`
/ `extractAssistantTextForPhase` (Telegram, mirror writes, session transcripts).
Discord just happens to be where #96849 was first observed.

## Root Cause

MiniMax-M3 emits internal monologue as plain `type: "text"` content blocks
interleaved with native `type: "thinking"` blocks, with no phase metadata:

```json
[
  { "type": "thinking", "thinking": "Gabe is asking me to confirm..." },
  { "type": "thinking", "thinking": "Excellent! Key info..." },
  { "type": "text",      "text":     "All done. Let me give Gabe a clean status update..." },
  { "type": "thinking", "thinking": "Let me give Gabe a tight summary..." },
  { "type": "thinking", "thinking": "Also, this message is the verification test..." },
  { "type": "text",      "text":     "Done. Here's the final status: ..." }
]
```

`sealNativeReasoningBeforeText()` in `openai-completions.ts` closes the open
thinking block when visible-text deltas begin, but it does not retroactively
mark the preceding text region as commentary. So `extractAssistantTextForPhase`
joined every unphased text block, concatenating the monologue with the final
answer. The Discord `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` / `stripReasoningTagsFromText`
pipeline is a no-op here because the monologue text contains no `<think>` tags.

Isolated sessions are unaffected because cron `agentTurn` doesn't use the
streaming subscription path — it reads payloads through a different lane that
doesn't depend on this extraction.

## Fix

Heuristic in `extractAssistantTextForPhase`: an unphased `text` block at
index `i` is treated as intermediate monologue iff there is a `thinking`
block at `j > i` AND another `text` block at `k > j`. That `text → thinking
→ text` shape is the smoking gun for provider-routed monologue — the model
talked, thought again, then produced its real answer.

Properties:
- `text → thinking` only (post-answer reflective thinking) → final text is preserved
- All-text content (no thinking blocks) → unchanged
- Messages with explicit phase metadata (`textSignature.phase`) → unchanged behavior
- `extractAssistantText` (no-phase variant used by `extractAssistantThinking`
  callers etc.) is intentionally untouched — that helper is consumed by paths
  that need the full text including monologue for replay/diagnostics

## Real Behavior Proof

Targeted unit tests pass; full Discord/Telegram delivery suites unaffected.

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/shared/chat-message-content.test.ts
 ✓ src/shared/chat-message-content.test.ts (19 tests) 2ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  19 passed (19)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-utils.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts
 ✓ src/agents/embedded-agent-utils.test.ts (48 tests) 11ms
 ✓ src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts (51 tests) 457ms
   Test Files  2 passed (2)
        Tests  99 passed (99)
```

Before (with the exact #96849 transcript shape): visible reply was
`"All done. Let me give Gabe a clean status update...\nDone. Here's the
final status: ..."`.

After: visible reply is `"Done. Here's the final status: ..."`.

## Regression Test Plan

Added to `src/shared/chat-message-content.test.ts` inside the
`extractAssistantVisibleText` describe block:

1. **`drops unphased text blocks emitted before a later thinking block`** —
   uses the exact 6-block transcript from the issue body. Asserts the visible
   text equals only the trailing `text` block (the final answer), never the
   earlier monologue text block.
2. **`keeps unphased final text even when a trailing thinking block follows`** —
   `thinking → text → thinking` shape. Asserts the text block is preserved
   (post-answer reflective thinking must not drop the final answer).
3. **`keeps all text when no thinking blocks are present`** — pure text-only
   content. Asserts joining behavior is unchanged when no thinking interleave
   exists.

The 16 pre-existing tests in the file continue to pass, including:
- final_answer-vs-commentary phase preference
- legacy unphased fallback when no phased blocks exist
- empty-final-answer non-fallback to legacy text

## Files Touched

- `src/shared/chat-message-content.ts` — heuristic added inside
  `extractAssistantTextForPhase`
- `src/shared/chat-message-content.test.ts` — 3 regression tests

Fixes #96849


---

## Update — round 2 (fabcd9a): fix on the actual delivery path

Thanks @clawsweeper for the P1 catch. You're right: the Discord main-session final delivery does **not** go through `src/shared/chat-message-content.ts` `extractAssistantTextForPhase`. It goes through `src/agents/embedded-agent-utils.ts` `extractAssistantVisibleText`, called from `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts`. The first patch only closed the shared/history path — not the hot path.

This round:

- Lifted the intermediate-monologue detector out of `chat-message-content.ts` into a shared export `isIntermediateMonologueTextBlock(content, index, hasExplicitPhasedTextBlocks)` — same heuristic (unphased `text` at index `i` is monologue iff a `thinking` block exists at `j > i` AND another `text` block exists at `k > j`), no logic drift.
- Reused it in `embedded-agent-utils.ts` `extractAssistantTextForPhase` so the delivery-path extractor drops the same blocks the shared extractor drops. No duplication.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/embedded-agent-utils.test.ts` using the **exact 6-block MiniMax-M3 transcript from #96849**, plus the two guard cases (`text -> thinking` only = keep; text-only = keep).

Local vitest (delivery-path + shared extractor):

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/shared/chat-message-content.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-utils.test.ts

 ✓ src/shared/chat-message-content.test.ts (19 tests) 1ms

      Tests  73 passed (73)
```

The new `#96849 delivery path` test fails against `main` and passes with this commit — that's the delivery-layer proof that the leak is closed at the extractor called by `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages`.

### On the "Real behavior proof" workflow

That CI check is label-gated and needs live Discord runtime capture, which I don't have credentials for locally. Please retrigger / grant the label once you're satisfied with the delivery-path unit test, or point me at the exact fixture format if you'd like this reproduced through a mocked transport rig instead.

target.title: fix(feishu): upgrade single newlines to double newlines for post+md rendering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu's post + tag: md message format treats single \n as a space (soft break), not a line break. Only \n\n (double newline) triggers a proper paragraph break. This causes all agent messages sent through the Feishu channel to appear with text "mashed together" when the markdown output uses standard single-newline separators, making long messages very difficult to read.

The fix adds normalizeFeishuNewlines() inside buildFeishuPostMessagePayload() so both sendMessageFeishu and editMessageFeishu paths benefit automatically.

Fixes #97074

## Code Changes

### v2: Markdown-aware normalization (current)

The normalizer is markdown-aware: it detects block-level structures (lists, blockquotes, ordered lists) and preserves their single newlines so Feishu renders them as continuous blocks rather than fragmented items.

**How it works (4-layer protection):**

1. Code fence pre-split -- shields fenced code blocks
2. Blank-line boundary split -- isolates markdown blocks
3. Marker detection per block -- identifies `-`, `*`, `+`, `\d+.`, `>` lines
4. Selective normalization -- plain paragraphs get \n\n, block structures keep \n

````typescript
function normalizeFeishuNewlines(text: string): string {
  const parts = text.split(/(```[\s\S]*?```)/g);
  for (let i = 0; i < parts.length; i += 2) {
    const segment = parts[i];
    if (!segment) { continue; }
    const blocks = segment.split(/\n\n+/);
    for (let j = 0; j < blocks.length; j++) {
      if (!/^\s*(?:[-*+]\s|\d+\.\s|>\s)/m.test(blocks[j])) {
        blocks[j] = blocks[j].replace(/(?<!\n)\n(?!\n)/g, "\n\n");
      }
    }
    parts[i] = blocks.join("\n\n");
  }
  return parts.join("");
}
````

**Input/Output matrix:**

| Input | v1 (blanket) | v2 (markdown-aware) |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| "Hello\nWorld" | "Hello\n\nWorld" | "Hello\n\nWorld" |
| "- A\n- B" | "- A\n\n- B" | "- A\n- B" |
| "> Q1\n> Q2" | "> Q1\n\n> Q2" | "> Q1\n> Q2" |
| "1. A\n2. B" | "1. A\n\n2. B" | "1. A\n2. B" |

### v1: Core normalization

```diff
-      text: messageText,
+      text: normalizeFeishuNewlines(messageText),
```

This single insertion at extensions/feishu/src/send.ts:627 covers both sendMessageFeishu and editMessageFeishu paths.

## Evidence

### Automated Tests

```
$ pnpm test --run extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
   Start at  20:49:19
   Duration  3.18s
```

12 test cases:

| Test | Category | Status |
|------|----------|--------|
| Upgrades single `\n` to `\n\n` | Core | PASS |
| Preserves existing `\n\n` | Core | PASS |
| Handles mixed single+double | Core | PASS |
| Preserves newlines in fenced code | Code blocks | PASS |
| Preserves unordered lists | Markdown-aware (v2) | PASS |
| Preserves ordered lists | Markdown-aware (v2) | PASS |
| Preserves blockquotes | Markdown-aware (v2) | PASS |
| Mixed paragraphs + lists | Markdown-aware (v2) | PASS |
| Indented list sub-items | Markdown-aware (v2) | PASS |
| Empty string | Edge case | PASS |
| No newlines passthrough | Edge case | PASS |
| Triple newline normalization | Edge case | PASS |

### Payload Verification (20 edge cases)

```
Core Fix Behavior:
  PASS: Single \n to \n\n (paragraph break)
  PASS: Existing \n\n preserved
  PASS: Mixed single + double newlines
  PASS: Triple newlines normalized
  PASS: Empty string
  PASS: Text without newlines (passthrough)

Code Block Preservation:
  PASS: Fenced code block preserved
  PASS: Multiple code blocks
  PASS: Code block at start
  PASS: Code block at end

Markdown Block Structures:
  PASS: Unordered list (-) preserved
  PASS: Unordered list (*) preserved
  PASS: Unordered list (+) preserved
  PASS: Ordered list preserved
  PASS: Blockquote preserved
  PASS: Mixed paragraphs + lists
  PASS: Indented list sub-items

Real-World Agent Output:
  PASS: Multi-paragraph message
  PASS: Message with list + code block
  PASS: Message with blockquote
```

### Full Extension Test Suite

```
$ pnpm test --run extensions/feishu/

 Test Files  71 passed, 1 failed
      Tests  974 passed, 1 failed
```

The single pre-existing failure (setup-surface.test.ts) is an unrelated i18n string mismatch, not caused by this PR.

### Edge Cases Covered

All verified edge cases pass: single \n upgrade, existing \n\n preservation, triple newline normalization, empty string, no newlines, fenced code blocks (start/mid/end), unordered lists (- * +), ordered lists, blockquotes, mixed paragraphs + lists, indented sub-items, and real-world multi-paragraph messages.

## Risk checklist

**Did user-visible behavior change?** (Yes)

- Feishu post+md messages will now render with proper paragraph breaks. Markdown block structures (lists, blockquotes, ordered lists) are detected and preserved.

**Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** (No)

**Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** (No)

- Security cleared by ClawSweeper. The diff is limited to Feishu message text normalization.

**What is the highest-risk area?**

- Messages with markdown that doesn't use blank-line separation before lists/blockquotes might not trigger the block detector.

**How is that risk mitigated?**

- 4-layer protection: code fence split, blank-line boundary split, per-block marker detection, selective normalization.
- AI-generated messages typically separate block structures with blank lines.
- The change is called only from buildFeishuPostMessagePayload.
- Feishu Card messages and other channels (Telegram, Slack) are unaffected.
"
